doc.description: Timestamp-only metadata on user and assistant messages. Supports absolute time and relative formats via Timestamp.

doc.name: ChatSendButton — Custom Icon
doc.description: Send buttons with custom icons via sendIcon and stopIcon props. Use to match the personality of the chat experience: a paper airplane for messaging, sparkles for AI generation, or a check mark for confirmation flows.

doc.name: ChatSendButton — In Composer
doc.description: Send button inside ChatComposer, where it reads state from context automatically. No wiring needed; the button enables when the input has content.

doc.name: ChatSendButton
doc.description: Ready, custom icon, and streaming states of the send button.

doc.name: ChatSendButton — States
doc.description: Disabled, ready, and streaming states at both sizes. The button automatically toggles between send (primary) and stop (secondary) based on streaming state.

doc.name: ChatSystemMessage
doc.description: System messages for date dividers, status updates, and informational notices. Shows both default and divider variants in a realistic conversation flow.

doc.name: ChatSystemMessage — Status Updates
doc.description: Realistic status messages in a conversation flow showing membership changes, timestamps, and resolution notices.

doc.name: ChatSystemMessage — Variants
doc.description: Default and divider variants side by side. Use default for inline status updates and divider for date separators or section breaks.

doc.name: ChatSystemMessage — Icon
doc.description: System messages with a leading icon that reinforces the message type. Use icons to help users scan and identify message categories at a glance.

doc.name: ChatTokenizedText — Basic
doc.description: A message with @mention tokens. Each matching pattern is replaced with its display name badge.

doc.name: ChatTokenizedText — Colors
doc.description: Tokens with different color variants to distinguish mentions, bugs, and features. Use variant colors to create a visual taxonomy: blue for people, red for bugs, green for features.

doc.name: ChatToolCalls — Expandable
doc.description: Tool calls with expandable result details showing diffs and command output in code blocks. Click a row to reveal its result.

doc.name: ChatToolCalls — Statuses
doc.description: All four status states (pending, running, complete, and error) shown together in a single group.

doc.name: ChatToolCalls — Simple
doc.description: A single inline tool call above a collapsible multi-call group with diff stats. Shows both layouts side by side.

doc.name: CheckboxInput — States
doc.description: Checkboxes with labels and descriptions in checked, unchecked, and disabled states. Each checkbox controls a single on/off setting. Add a description to explain what the setting does.

doc.name: CheckboxInput — Indeterminate
doc.description: A "select all" checkbox that controls a group of options. When only some options are checked, it shows a dash instead of a checkmark. Clicking it checks or unchecks everything.

doc.name: CheckboxInput
doc.description: Interactive checkboxes showing checked, unchecked, and indeterminate states with descriptions.

doc.name: CheckboxInput — Status
doc.description: Checkboxes with error, warning, and success validation messages. Use the status prop to show feedback after form validation: errors block submission, warnings inform, and success confirms.

doc.name: CheckboxList — Select All With Indeterminate
doc.description: A "select all" toggle at the top of a checkbox list that switches to an indeterminate dash when only some items are checked, useful for bulk actions like exporting documents or assigning permissions where users often want everything at once.

doc.name: CheckboxList — With End Content
doc.description: Badges in the trailing slot show contextual info, like a price or status, next to each option without cluttering the label, so users can compare choices at a glance.

doc.name: CheckboxListItem — Basic
doc.description: Checkbox items with labels and descriptions inside a controlled CheckboxList. Use for multi-select option groups like notification preferences.

doc.name: CheckboxListItem
doc.description: Checkbox list items with labels, descriptions, and different states including disabled.

doc.name: Citation — Inline Text
doc.description: Citations embedded within a paragraph of text, showing how they flow inline with surrounding content.

doc.name: Citation — Showcase
doc.description: All citation variants at a glance: label chips and numbered badges, with and without icons and links.

doc.name: Citation — Source List
doc.description: A list of citation sources with icons, as you might show at the end of an AI-generated response or article footer.

doc.name: Code — Text Sizes
doc.description: Inline code rendered inside heading, body, supporting, and label text. Code automatically matches the font size of its parent text element.

doc.name: Code — Inline
doc.description: Inline code references mixed within a paragraph of body text. Use Code to mark up function names, hooks, or API terms so they stand out from surrounding prose.

doc.name: Code
doc.description: Inline code snippets inside a sentence showing how Code renders alongside body text.

doc.name: Code — Content Types
doc.description: Inline code used for variables, terminal commands, CSS properties, file paths, and keyboard shortcuts. Shows how Code adapts to different kinds of technical content.

doc.name: Code — Snippet
doc.description: Short terminal commands with no header: the copy button sits in its own column beside the code, so a one-line command reads as a single row and a long line ends before the button instead of running under it. Use for install instructions or one-liner commands that readers will paste directly.

doc.name: Code — Highlighted
doc.description: TypeScript code with specific lines highlighted to draw attention to a key section. Use highlightLines to call out new or important code in tutorials and changelogs.

doc.name: Code — Config
doc.description: A JSON configuration file with a title bar and line numbers. The title prop adds a filename label in the header so readers know which file the code belongs to.

doc.name: Code — Scrollable
doc.description: A long code block with a max height that enables vertical scrolling. Use maxHeight to keep the block from dominating the page when displaying large files.

doc.name: CodeBlock
doc.description: A syntax-highlighted TypeScript code block with line numbers, a title bar, and a copy button.

doc.name: Code — Terminal
doc.description: A dark terminal-style command block: a bash CodeBlock wrapped in SyntaxTheme with the GitHub Dark preset, copy button on, and no line numbers. Use for shell sessions or CLI output that should read as a terminal even on light pages. Reach for a dark syntax preset instead of hand-rolling a dark box with custom CSS.

doc.name: Collapsible — Controlled
doc.description: Manage the open section from parent state, so something other than a click can move it: a URL parameter, a form jumping to the step that failed validation, or the Previous/Next controls shown here. onChange hands back the whole open value.

doc.name: Collapsible — FAQ
doc.description: FAQ built with hasDividers: row hairlines and density padding with no custom CSS. Questions set their own type — body at semibold, not the trigger's default 17px large — so a list of questions reads as rows rather than a stack of headings, and question and answer separate on weight and color instead of size.

doc.name: useCollapsible — Custom Disclosure
doc.description: Custom disclosure UI built directly with useCollapsible for headless open/close state.

doc.name: Collapsible — Multiple Mode
doc.description: Several sections open at once, for comparing across them — feature lists, pricing tiers. One Collapsible per Card, so each trigger keeps its own large type: it is the heading of its surface, not a row in a list.

doc.name: Collapsible
doc.description: An accordion group with three collapsible sections in single mode: opening one closes the others.

doc.name: Collapsible — Single Mode
doc.description: Only one section open at a time, so a single body of content competes for attention. Use defaultValue to pre-expand whichever section a first-time reader needs. Each Collapsible owns a Section, so its trigger is that section heading.

doc.name: Collapsible — With Dividers
doc.description: A flat list on the page background with hand-placed Dividers, for detail panels and sidebars where cards would add too much weight. Rows, so the triggers step down to body-semibold and a supporting metadata line sits under each answer.

doc.name: CollapsibleGroup — Density
doc.description: density sets the block padding on every row in the group, so a list of sections can be tuned to the surface it sits on without touching the rows. compact for dense surfaces like sidebars and inspectors, balanced (the default) for page content, spacious for a short list that is the main thing on the page. It follows Table's scale and pairs with hasDividers, which turns it on at balanced.

doc.name: CollapsibleGroup
doc.description: CollapsibleGroup coordinates its Collapsible children: with type="single", opening one closes the others. No state or handlers in the example — the group owns which value is open and each child only declares its own. One Collapsible per Card, so each trigger keeps its default large type as the heading of its own surface.

doc.name: CommandPalette — Async Search
doc.description: Server-side search with loading spinner and custom empty states.

doc.name: CommandPalette — Grouped
doc.description: Command palette with items grouped via auxiliaryData.group.

doc.name: CommandPalette — Custom Footer
doc.description: Command palette with a custom footer tip message.

doc.name: CommandPalette — Picker Mode
doc.description: Single-value picker with persistent selection and check indicator.

doc.name: CommandPalette — Rich Items
doc.description: Custom item rendering with icons, keyboard shortcuts, and keyword search.

doc.name: CommandPalette
doc.description: Basic command palette with static items and keyboard navigation.

doc.name: CommandPaletteEmpty — Basic
doc.description: A command palette with no results, showing a custom empty message via emptyBootstrapText. Use to explain why the palette is empty and what the user can do next.

doc.name: CommandPaletteEmpty
doc.description: Command palette empty state shown when no commands are available.

doc.name: CommandPaletteFooter — Basic
doc.description: A command palette footer with no children, rendering the built-in keyboard navigation hints. Use CommandPaletteFooter without content to get the default arrow-key, Enter, and Esc hints below the results list.

doc.name: CommandPaletteFooter
doc.description: Command palette footer with custom tip content.

doc.name: CommandPaletteGroup — Basic
doc.description: Command palette items organized under group headings using the composed CommandPaletteGroup form. Use to separate related commands into labeled sections.

doc.name: CommandPaletteGroup
doc.description: Command palette groups in both data-driven (auxiliaryData.group) and composed (CommandPaletteGroup + CommandPaletteItem) forms.

doc.name: CommandPaletteInput — With End Content
doc.description: Custom placeholder and a keyboard shortcut badge in the trailing slot via endContent.

doc.name: CommandPaletteInput
doc.description: Command palette search input with a custom placeholder and a keyboard shortcut hint in the endContent slot.

doc.name: CommandPaletteItem — Basic
doc.description: Selectable command palette items inside a CommandPaletteList, including highlighted and disabled states. Use when composing a palette manually instead of a search source.

doc.name: CommandPaletteItem
doc.description: An inline command palette whose items pair each command label with its keyboard shortcut through renderItem.

doc.name: CommandPaletteList — Item States
doc.description: Flat list showing the highlighted, selected, and disabled item states. Use CommandPaletteGroup to add section headings.

doc.name: CommandPaletteList
doc.description: Scrollable command palette list with grouped items, including a highlighted item, composed without a full CommandPalette.

doc.name: ComplexSelector — Deadline Picker
doc.description: A multi-step deadline field: pick a preset like Today or Next week, or switch to a custom date and time before applying. The popup stays open until the user commits, so the content owns the Apply action.

doc.name: ComplexSelector
doc.description: A two-axis picker: choose a fruit and a ripeness level from one control. ComplexSelector owns the trigger, popover, and focus restore while the custom grid owns its keyboard semantics.

doc.name: ComplexSelector — Tree Search
doc.description: A destination picker that combines a search field with a TreeList hierarchy. TreeList owns tree keyboard navigation; ComplexSelector owns the trigger, popover, and focus restore. Selecting a folder closes the popup.

doc.name: ContextMenu — Basic
doc.description: An adaptive context area: long-press opens a BottomSheet on compact touch screens, while right-click opens a cursor-positioned menu elsewhere.

doc.name: ContextMenu — Bottom Sheet
doc.description: A ContextMenu using the explicit BottomSheet presentation. Long-press the target on touch devices or right-click it with a pointer. Keep a visible menu trigger for important mobile actions.

doc.name: ContextMenu
doc.description: An adaptive context area that supports long-press on compact touch screens and right-click elsewhere.

doc.name: ContextMenuItem — Basic
doc.description: Context menu items with labels and secondary descriptions. Use ContextMenuItem to render custom menu entries with consistent styling.

doc.name: ContextMenuItem
doc.description: Context menu with custom-rendered items using ContextMenuItem for icons and descriptions.

doc.name: DateInput — Clearable
doc.description: Date input with a clear button that resets the value. Use when the date field is optional and the user may need to undo their selection.

doc.name: DateInput — Min/Max Constraints
doc.description: Date input constrained to a min/max window. Use when only certain dates are valid, like booking availability or a fiscal quarter.

doc.name: DateInput — Formats
doc.description: The format prop reuses Timestamp's format vocabulary to control how the committed value is displayed: date, date_long (default), date_weekday, and system_date, or a function for a fully custom string. Formatting applies only to the committed value, never to text the user is actively typing.

doc.name: DateInput
doc.description: A date input field with a calendar popover. Type a date or click the calendar icon to pick one.

doc.name: DateInput — Description
doc.description: Date input with helper text below the label explaining what the field expects. Use when the purpose of the date is not obvious from the label alone.

doc.name: DateInput — Validation
doc.description: Date input in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface validation issues, caution the user, or confirm a valid selection.

doc.name: DateRangeInput
doc.description: A date range picker with a button trigger and dual-month calendar popover with preset ranges.

doc.name: DateRangeInput — With Presets
doc.description: Date range picker with quick-select presets for common periods. Use for analytics dashboards, report filters, or any context where users frequently select standard time windows.

doc.name: DateRangeInput — Validation
doc.description: Date range input in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface booking conflicts, flag high-demand periods, or confirm an available range.

doc.name: DateTimeInput
doc.description: A combined date and time picker. Desktop opens a calendar popover with a time input; touch devices open a Date/Time bottom sheet.

doc.name: DateTimeInput — Validation
doc.description: DateTimeInput in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface scheduling conflicts, caution the user about edge cases, or confirm a valid datetime.

doc.name: Dialog — Adaptive presentation
doc.description: Opt-in recipe for an AdaptiveDialog wrapper: Dialog remains the default everywhere, while touchPresentation="bottom-sheet" switches only at lg and below when pointer is coarse and hover is unavailable. Includes a deterministic presentation override for tests/unusual environments and notes that BottomSheet purpose controls swipe and scrim dismissal. Usage examples: touchPresentation="dialog" keeps Dialog, "fullscreen" chooses fullscreen Dialog, and "bottom-sheet" chooses BottomSheet only for the touch-oriented range. Keep presentation as the deterministic override. Do not use this by default for AlertDialog or destructive confirmations.

doc.name: Dialog — Confirmation
doc.description: Asks the user to confirm a destructive action before it happens. Use before deleting projects, removing team members, revoking API keys, or any irreversible operation.

doc.name: Dialog — Form
doc.description: Collects user input without navigating away from the page. Uses purpose="form" so clicking the backdrop won't close it. Use for editing profiles, creating items, or updating settings inline.

doc.name: Dialog — Fullscreen
doc.description: Takes over the entire viewport for content that needs maximum space. Use for documentation viewers, rich text editors, multi-step wizards, or media previews where the standard dialog width is too narrow.

doc.name: Dialog — Scrollable
doc.description: Constrains the dialog height and scrolls the body when content overflows. Use for terms and conditions, license agreements, changelogs, or any long-form content the user needs to review before accepting.

doc.name: Dialog
doc.description: Modal dialog with a header, body content, and close button.

doc.name: Dialog — Required
doc.description: Cannot be dismissed by Escape or backdrop click; the user must explicitly choose an action. Uses purpose="required". Use for ownership transfers, legal acknowledgements, or critical decisions where skipping is not an option.

doc.name: DialogHeader — Basic
doc.description: A DialogHeader with a title, subtitle, and close button, placed in the header slot of a Dialog Layout. Pass onOpenChange to render the close button.

doc.name: DialogHeader
doc.description: DialogHeader provides a structured header for dialogs with slots for title, subtitle, close button, and optional start or end content.

doc.name: Divider — Full Bleed
doc.description: Divider that extends past container padding to span the full width. Use inside cards or panels when you want a clean edge-to-edge separation, like between an order summary and total.

doc.name: Divider — Variants
doc.description: Horizontal dividers in subtle and strong variants, plus a labeled divider. A quick visual reference for separator styles.

doc.name: Divider — Variants
doc.description: Subtle, labeled, and strong dividers in a single card. Use subtle between related sections, labeled for alternatives like "or", and strong for high-contrast boundaries.

doc.name: Divider — Vertical
doc.description: Vertical dividers separating side-by-side metrics. Use between stat cards, toolbar groups, or any horizontal layout where you need a visual boundary between sections.

doc.name: Edit form with footer actions
doc.description: Compose a Layout with DrawerHeader, the fields in LayoutContent, and Cancel and Save in a pinned LayoutFooter. purpose="form" keeps Escape but ignores scrim clicks, so a stray click outside does not discard edits.

doc.name: Modal or non-modal (hasScrim)
doc.description: The default modal drawer dims the page, traps focus, and closes on a scrim click. With hasScrim={false}, the drawer has no scrim or focus trap and leaves the page interactive.

doc.name: Basic
doc.description: Open a modal drawer from a single trigger. The scrim dims the page; Escape, a scrim click, or the header close button closes it, and focus returns to the trigger.

doc.name: Slide in from the start edge
doc.displayName: Slide in from the start edge
doc.description: Set side="start" to open from the inline start edge: left in LTR and right in RTL. The default end edge follows the inspector convention.

doc.name: Width budget: pixels or any CSS length
doc.displayName: Width budget: pixels or any CSS length
doc.description: Compare a numeric pixel width with rem and percentage lengths. The width budget also caps the drawer on mobile.

doc.name: DrawerHeader
doc.description: DrawerHeader provides a structured header for drawers with slots for title, subtitle, close button, and optional start or end content.

doc.name: With subtitle and end content
doc.description: Add a subtitle under the title and put a status, such as a Badge, in endContent. The close button stays at the end of the row.

doc.name: With close button
doc.description: Pass onOpenChange to render a close button that calls it with false. Drawer renders no close button of its own, so this is the usual visible way to close.

doc.name: DropdownMenu — Actions
doc.description: Action menu with dividers separating safe and destructive operations. Use for row-level actions on items like documents, projects, or records.

doc.name: DropdownMenu — Adaptive presentation
doc.description: Chooses a bottom sheet for compact touch surfaces and an anchored popover otherwise. The media query is product policy, while DropdownMenu owns both presentations.

doc.name: DropdownMenu — Icon Trigger
doc.description: Overflow menu triggered by an icon-only button with no chevron or label text. Use for row-level actions in tables, cards, or lists where a text button would take too much space.

doc.name: DropdownMenu
doc.description: A button that opens a dropdown menu with action items. The menu starts open for preview.

doc.name: DropdownMenu — Disabled
doc.description: Menu with selectively disabled items based on permissions. Use when some actions require higher privileges, like admin-only operations.

doc.name: DropdownMenu — Sections
doc.description: Menu items organized into titled sections for easy scanning. Use when you have 6+ actions that fall into distinct categories, like Create vs Manage.

doc.name: DropdownMenu — Submenu
doc.description: Action menu with a nested submenu. Hover or Right arrow opens the flyout; Left arrow / Escape closes it. Use to group related destinations or secondary actions without crowding the top level.

doc.name: DropdownMenuGroup
doc.description: A compound-mode menu whose rows are titled in groups. Each DropdownMenuGroup renders a role="group" named by its heading; arrow keys and typeahead skip the heading.

doc.name: DropdownMenuGroup — Selectable rows
doc.description: Titled groups around a radio group and checkbox rows — the rows the data API cannot express, which is why the heading lives in compound mode.

doc.name: DropdownMenuItem — Basic
doc.description: Dropdown menu items with labels and secondary descriptions. Use DropdownMenuItem to render custom menu entries with consistent styling.

doc.name: DropdownMenuItem
doc.description: Dropdown menu with custom-rendered items using DropdownMenuItem for icons and descriptions.

doc.name: EmptyState — Actions
doc.description: Full empty state with icon, message, and action buttons. Use when a search returns no results, a filter clears all items, or a list has been emptied. The buttons give the user a way forward: go back, clear filters, or try a different query.

doc.name: EmptyState — Compact
doc.description: Smaller empty state with reduced spacing for constrained areas. Use inside sidebar panels, card widgets, or notification drawers where a full-size empty state would overwhelm the layout.

doc.name: EmptyState — Container
doc.description: Empty state wrapped in a Card for first-time setup or onboarding. Use when the user has not created any items yet, like a project list, team roster, or dashboard widget that will fill with data once they take action.

doc.name: EmptyState
doc.description: A no-results empty state with an icon, descriptive message, and a call-to-action button.

doc.name: Field — Required & Optional
doc.description: Required and optional field indicators side by side. Use isRequired on fields the user must fill in, and isOptional to clarify which fields can be skipped.

doc.name: Field
doc.description: A form field wrapping a text input with a label, description, and validation status.

doc.name: Field — Validation States
doc.description: All three validation states: error, warning, and success. Use error for invalid input, warning for potential issues like reserved names, and success to confirm valid entries like API keys.

doc.name: Field — Description
doc.description: Fields with helper text below the label. Use descriptions to explain format requirements, constraints, or what happens with the data, like "At least 8 characters" or "We will send a confirmation link".

doc.name: FieldLabel — Basic
doc.description: Standalone labels with required and optional indicators and a helper description. Use when labeling a custom control that does not render its own label.

doc.name: FieldLabel
doc.description: Standalone field labels demonstrating required, optional, tooltip, and icon variations.

doc.name: FieldStatus — Basic
doc.description: Detached error and success messages for validation feedback. Use below checkboxes, switches, or custom controls where an attached status would overlap.

doc.name: FieldStatus
doc.description: Field status messages in error, warning, and success states with attached and detached variants.

doc.name: FileInput — Basic
doc.description: A controlled single-file upload with accepted types, a size limit, and helper text. Use for standard document upload fields in forms.

doc.name: FormLayout — Horizontal
doc.description: Two fields side by side for naturally paired inputs like first and last name

doc.name: FormLayout — Settings Form
doc.description: Settings form with labels placed beside their inputs

doc.name: FormLayout — Mixed Controls
doc.description: Form with different control types: text input, selector, and checkboxes

doc.name: FormLayout — Nested Address Form
doc.description: Address form mixing vertical and horizontal layouts for grouped fields

doc.name: FormLayout
doc.description: A vertical form layout with text input fields.

doc.name: Grid — Dashboard Layout
doc.description: Dashboard layout with mixed-size widgets and a full-width summary row

doc.name: Grid — Card Gallery
doc.description: Card gallery with responsive columns that maintain consistent widths

doc.name: Grid — Responsive Auto-Fit
doc.description: Responsive grid where cards stretch to fill remaining space

doc.name: Grid — Column Spanning
doc.description: Grid with featured items spanning multiple columns and rows

doc.name: GridSpan — Columns
doc.description: Grid items spanning two of three columns. Wrap a grid child in GridSpan to make it occupy multiple columns for asymmetric layouts.

doc.name: GridSpan
doc.description: GridSpan lets a grid item span multiple columns or rows within an Grid, enabling masonry-style and asymmetric layouts.

doc.name: HStack — Basic
doc.description: Items arranged in a horizontal row with a consistent gap and centered vertical alignment. Use HStack whenever siblings should sit side by side.

doc.name: HStack
doc.description: Demonstrates HStack arranging items horizontally with different gaps and alignments.

doc.name: Heading — Card Grid
doc.description: Responsive card grid with truncated headings and descriptions for uniform layout

doc.name: Heading — Page Hierarchy
doc.description: Real-world page layout demonstrating heading levels h1 through h3 with supporting text

doc.name: Heading — Truncation
doc.description: Single-line and multi-line heading truncation with ellipsis for constrained layouts

doc.name: useAnnounce — Filter Result Count
doc.description: A product filter that announces its result count with useAnnounce: once typing pauses for 500 ms, a screen reader hears "3 results" or "No results". The count has its own hasReplace instance, as the hook's docs advise for a changing value.

doc.name: useClickableContainer — Clickable Project Card
doc.description: A project card that useClickableContainer makes clickable anywhere: a click on the card follows its title link, while the Star button, the owner link and a text selection keep their own behavior, and Ctrl/Cmd+click or middle-click opens the project in a new tab.

doc.name: useClipboard — Share Link
doc.description: A share card that copies its invite link with useClipboard: the Copy button reads "Copied" while isCopied is true, a screen reader hears "Link copied", and a second press restarts the reset timer.

doc.name: useCollator — Locale-aware Name Sort
doc.description: A list of names sorted with the compare function from useCollator: accented and lowercase names land where a reader expects, and switching the provider locale to Swedish moves Å and Ö after Z.

doc.name: useContainerReveal — Reveal-on-hover Row Actions
doc.description: File rows keep their edit/delete actions hidden at rest and reveal them on hover or keyboard focus via useContainerReveal; the actions stay mounted and in the tab order.

doc.name: useFocusTrap — Quick Edit Panel
doc.description: A custom quick-edit panel, not built on Dialog, that traps focus with useFocusTrap: focusFirst moves focus to its field on open, Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside it, Escape closes it through onEscape, and closing returns focus to the Quick edit button.

doc.name: useGridFocus — Color Swatch Grid
doc.description: A color swatch picker in rows of eight with one Tab stop. useGridFocus moves focus with the arrow keys, Home and End, and Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End. Each swatch is a button, so Enter or a click picks it.

doc.name: useHotkeys — Search and Help Shortcuts
doc.description: Page shortcuts registered with useHotkeys: "/" focuses the search field and "?" opens the shortcut help, while typing either character in the field just types it. A switch turns the single-key shortcuts off through isDisabled.

doc.name: useImageMode — Photo Caption
doc.description: A photo banner with a caption over the sky. useImageMode samples only the strip under the caption and MediaTheme switches the caption between light and dark text from the result. A Beach photo switch swaps a night photo for a bright beach photo, and while the new photo loads the caption keeps the dark fallback.

doc.name: useInputContainer — Search Field Wrapper
doc.description: A custom search field wrapper with a leading search icon, padding and a trailing Clear button. useInputContainer puts focus in the input when the icon or the padding is clicked, while a click on Clear empties the field without the wrapper taking it over.

doc.name: useInputStatusIcon — Coupon Code Status
doc.description: A custom bordered coupon-code input whose status affordance comes from useInputStatusIcon. A wrong code shows the error status and SAVE20 shows success. Switching the variant moves between a plain glyph with a message below (attached), no icon on the field (detached), and a focusable button whose tooltip keyboard and screen-reader users can reach, with its aria-describedby id returned by the hook (tooltip).

doc.name: useInteractiveRole — One Tile, Four Roles
doc.description: A polymorphic Tile used four ways: with an href it renders as a link, with an onClick as a button, with neither as plain content, and placed as a Popover trigger it becomes the trigger button through context — the resolution order in one place.

doc.name: useKeyboardHint — Arrow-key Hint
doc.description: A custom five-star rating with one Tab stop calls useKeyboardHint directly: tabbing into it shows a "← → to navigate" hint, the first arrow press dismisses it, and tabbing back in does not show it again.

doc.name: useListFocus — Recent Files
doc.description: A "Recent files" list of buttons with keyboard navigation from useListFocus: ArrowUp and ArrowDown move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last row, focus wraps at the ends, and only one row is in the tab order.

doc.name: useLocale — Invoice Summary
doc.description: An invoice summary that formats its date and amount with Intl using the locale from useLocale, so switching the provider from English to German changes "Nov 2, 2026" and "$1,234.50" to "2. Nov. 2026" and "1.234,50 $" with no second locale source.

doc.name: useMergedRefs — AutoGrowTextArea
doc.description: An AutoGrowTextArea that forwards the caller's ref and also keeps its own ref to measure scrollHeight. The merged ref attaches both to the same textarea: it resizes itself while a parent button focuses it through the forwarded ref.

doc.name: useOverflow — Editor Toolbar
doc.description: Resize the card: useOverflow moves the toolbar actions that do not fit into a More menu, and shows them again when the card gets wider.

doc.name: usePressFeedback — Pressable Card
doc.description: A Card made pressable with usePressFeedback: its marker and the interactionOverlayStyles backgroundImage overlay go straight on the Card, so a press darkens the card the way every Astryx pressable does; focusOutlineStyles.focusVisible gives it the shared Astryx focus ring for keyboard focus; and a click, Enter or Space flips it.

doc.name: useScrollLock — Full-screen Mobile Menu
doc.description: A custom full-screen menu opened from a Menu button. useScrollLock pins the page behind it while it is open, so the page does not scroll or shift sideways, and closing the menu returns the reader to the same scroll position.

doc.name: useScrollOverflow — Filter Strip Edge Fades
doc.description: A row of active filters that scrolls sideways. useScrollOverflow reports which edge has hidden filters, and the strip fades only that edge: none while every filter fits, the end at the start, both mid-scroll and the start at the end. Adding or removing a filter updates the fades, and in a right-to-left layout the start edge is on the right.

doc.name: useScrollableArea — Activity Log Panel
doc.description: A fixed-height Activity log panel whose entries scroll up and down. useScrollableArea makes the panel a keyboard tab stop only when its entries overflow, reports which edges have more entries so a top or bottom shadow shows only there, and keeps a scroll that reaches the end from scrolling the page. Add entry flips the panel from not scrollable to scrollable.

doc.name: useStreamingText — Streaming Response
doc.description: A chat-style reply card: while the response streams in bursts, useStreamingText reveals it steadily character by character; when streaming ends the full text snaps into place. Regenerate replays the stream.

doc.name: useTranslator — Load More Footer
doc.description: A "Load more" footer under a list that gets its button label and its "Showing 3 of 9" count from the function useTranslator returns, with app message keys supplied per locale through InternationalizationProvider, so switching the provider to French changes both strings.

doc.name: useTreeFocus — Keyboard File Tree
doc.description: A custom file tree built from plain rows with tree roles. useTreeFocus gives it the WAI-ARIA tree keyboard model: ArrowUp and ArrowDown move over the visible rows, ArrowRight opens a folder or moves into it, ArrowLeft closes it or moves to its parent, Home and End jump to the ends, a typed letter jumps to a matching name, Enter opens a file, and only one row is in the tab order.

doc.name: useTypeahead — Type to Focus a Country
doc.displayName: useTypeahead — Type to Focus a Country
doc.description: A country list of buttons with useListFocus arrow keys and useTypeahead type-to-focus. Typing "can" focuses Canada, pressing "b" again and again cycles through Belgium, Brazil and Bulgaria, and "e" finds Éire with the accent ignored. The hook only reports the match through onMatch, and useListFocus moves focus.

doc.name: useHoverCard — Profile Preview

doc.description: Buttons positioned at the start, center, and end of a row.

doc.name: Stack — Directions
doc.description: Badges arranged horizontally and vertically in side-by-side cards.

doc.name: Stack — Fill Item
doc.description: An avatar, text, and button in a row; the text stretches to fill the available space.

doc.name: StackItem — Fill
doc.description: A static-width item next to one that fills the remaining space. Wrap stack children in StackItem when an item needs explicit sizing control.

doc.name: StackItem
doc.description: StackItem can be used within HStack or VStack for more granular control over individual item sizing and alignment, but is optional; stack children work without it.

doc.name: StatusDot — Pulsing
doc.description: Animated pulsing dots for live, processing, and error states.

doc.name: StatusDot
doc.description: A positive status dot indicator.

doc.name: StatusDot — Status Indicators
doc.description: Labeled status dot list for presence indicators like online, away, and offline.

doc.name: StatusDot — Variants
doc.description: All five semantic color variants displayed in a row.

doc.name: Step — Content Slot
doc.description: Children passed to a Step render below its description, indented to line up with the label rather than the indicator, and stay outside the clickable label area so buttons inside remain their own targets. In a full flow you gate the slot on the step being active. That is what turns a vertical stepper into an expanding one.

doc.name: Step — Indicator
doc.description: Everything the indicator prop accepts: the auto default, an always-number badge, a custom ReactNode, and none, each on its own completed Step so the prop is the only difference between them. Every variant occupies the same 16px box, so a step swapping its number for a check as it completes never shifts the label beside it. The last cell shows that a custom node can be live rather than static: a Spinner on a step that is in progress, shaded `inherit` so it picks up the step's own tint like any other glyph.

doc.name: Step
doc.description: A single Step, with every part it can render: the indicator, the label with its optional marker and trailing endContent, and the description beneath. A Step never sets its own completed/current state. It declares its index and derives the rest from the parent Stepper, so one Step in one Stepper is a complete example.

doc.name: Step — States
doc.description: Every state a single Step can land in, each shown as one Step in its own Stepper. Completed, current, and upcoming are derived by comparing the step index against the parent activeStep, so they are never set directly; isDisabled and status are the two a step declares itself. Status is a separate axis from progress, which is why a completed step can still carry a warning.

doc.name: Stepper — Custom Content
doc.description: A vertical stepper where each step owns a slice of the page. The content slot takes any node (form fields, a summary panel, a banner), so a stepper is not limited to multi-step forms. Rendering the slot only for the active step is what makes the flow expand one step at a time.

doc.name: Stepper — Indicator Modes
doc.description: The indicator prop side by side: none (the bar and label carry the progress on their own), auto (check when done, ring when current, number ahead), always-number, and a custom icon per step.

doc.name: Stepper — On-Track Horizontal
doc.description: The on-track layout in horizontal orientation: instead of sitting beside the label, each indicator is slotted into the connector itself, so the numbered nodes read as beads on one continuous line. Labels center under their node.

doc.name: Stepper — On-Track Vertical
doc.description: The on-track layout in vertical orientation: indicators sit inline on a continuous connector rail, with each label and description beside its node. Compare with the separated layout, where the indicator sits alongside its own bar segment instead of on a shared rail.

doc.name: Stepper — Checkout Progress
doc.description: The default stepper: a horizontal track where every step owns an equal segment of the progress bar above its label. The default auto indicator resolves itself per step: a check once the step is done, a ring on the current step, a number for the ones still ahead. Click any step to jump.

doc.name: Stepper — Validation Status
doc.description: Semantic status per step in a verification flow: success shows a green check, error a red glyph, accent the in-progress step. Status sets the indicator color and glyph only, never the connector, and is announced to assistive tech as text.

doc.name: Stepper — Horizontal Narrow Collapsed
doc.description: A narrow horizontal stepper using horizontalOptions. At 320px wide, four steps fall below the 112px minimumStepWidth and collapse into a current-step summary with Previous and Next controls.

doc.name: Switch — Disabled
doc.description: Disabled switch with label and description for gated features.

doc.name: Switch — Settings Panel
doc.description: Settings panel with spread-spaced switches in a card.

doc.name: Switch
doc.description: A toggle switch for enabling notifications.

doc.name: Switch — With Description
doc.description: Toggle with a label and supporting description text.

doc.name: Switch — With Status
doc.description: Switches with error, warning, and success validation states.

doc.name: SyntaxTheme — Dark Preset
doc.description: Wrap a code block in SyntaxTheme to apply a dark syntax preset such as Dracula.

doc.name: SyntaxTheme — Light Preset
doc.description: Use a light syntax preset for code examples that need to sit on light documentation surfaces.

doc.name: SyntaxTheme — Compact Preset
doc.description: A concise code block rendered with the One Dark Pro syntax preset to show how SyntaxTheme changes highlighting colors without making the page long.

doc.name: Tab
doc.description: Tab is an individual tab item within a TabList, supporting labels, icons, selected icons, and end content slots.

doc.name: Tab — Selected Icon
doc.description: A tab that changes its icon when selected.

doc.name: TabList — Fill Layout
doc.description: Tabs that stretch to fill the available width with a bottom divider.

doc.name: TabList — With Actions
doc.description: Page header pattern with tabs on the left and action buttons pushed to the right. When hasDivider is true, match the Button size to the TabList size so the tabs and actions align to a shared baseline above the divider.

doc.name: TabList — With Badge
doc.description: Tabs with notification badge counts rendered via endContent. Uses error variant for urgent counts and neutral for informational ones.

doc.name: TabList — With Icons
doc.description: Tabs with leading icons alongside text labels.

doc.name: TabList — With Overflow Menu
doc.description: Tab list with a dropdown menu for additional items that do not fit inline.

doc.name: TabList — With Status Dot
doc.description: Tabs with status dot indicators rendered via endContent to show live environment health at a glance.

doc.name: TabMenu — Basic
doc.description: An overflow menu at the end of a TabList that collects secondary tabs behind a dropdown. Use it when there are more tabs than fit comfortably inline.

doc.name: TabMenu
doc.description: TabMenu is an overflow menu within a TabList that groups additional tab options into a dropdown, showing the selected option's label as the trigger text.

doc.name: useTableColumnResize — Draggable Columns
doc.description: A Table using useTableColumnResize. Drag the right edge of any column header to resize; widths are committed on release. The last proportional column flexes to fill remaining space.

doc.name: useTableRowsVirtualization - Fixed Height Rows
doc.description: A Table with 1,000 product rows in a fixed-height viewport. Scroll vertically to mount the visible rows. The caller keeps all data and columns; this hook does not virtualize columns.

doc.name: useTableStickyColumns — Pinned Columns
doc.description: A Table using useTableStickyColumns to pin the Name column to the start edge and Status to the end edge. Scroll horizontally; pinned columns stay in view with a soft shadow over the scrolling content.

doc.name: Table: Bulk Actions
doc.description: Controlled row selection with the reusable TableSelectionToolbar rendered in flow above the table. Product actions occupy the logical start; synchronized selection count and complete clear action occupy the logical end.

doc.name: Table — Column Settings
doc.description: Table with a column visibility picker in the toolbar. Toggle columns on and off.

doc.name: Table — Popover Filters
doc.description: Table with popover filter controls triggered by icons in column headers.

doc.name: Table: Floating Bulk Actions
doc.description: The reusable TableSelectionToolbar inside a capped, self-contained scroll region for a long non-sticky table below metric cards. The caller-owned sticky placement keeps actions 16px from the example scrollport without moving the table when selection changes.

doc.name: Table — Grid Dividers
doc.description: Compact table with grid dividers showing both row and column borders, suited for dense numeric data.

doc.name: useTableGroupedRows — Collapsible Groups
doc.description: A table grouped into collapsible sections with useTableGroupedRows. Each group gets a full-width header with a chevron, label, and member count; click to collapse/expand.

doc.name: Table — In Card
doc.description: Table composed inside a card with a heading, demonstrating container bleed alignment.

doc.name: Table — Inline Filters
doc.description: Table with inline filter controls rendered directly below each column header.

doc.name: Table — Selection in the Leading Mark
doc.displayName: Table — Selection in the Leading Mark
doc.description: Selection without a checkbox column: each item shows its avatar, and the checkbox takes the avatar slot while a mouse is over it, on keyboard focus, and everywhere once anything is selected; on touch screens it always shows. The state comes from useTableSelectionState, and the checkboxes render in the name column instead of the useTableSelection column, so checked items get no aria-selected or highlight; add them if needed.

doc.name: Table — Paginated Data
doc.description: Paginated data table navigating through a larger dataset page by page.

doc.name: Table — Resizable Columns
doc.description: Table with draggable column resize handles. Drag the right edge of any header to resize.

doc.name: Table — Rich Cell Content
doc.description: Table with rich cell content using Link for emails and Badge for role labels.

doc.name: useTableRowExpansion — Tree Table
doc.description: A tree table using useTableRowExpansion with inherited columns. Child rows use the same columns as parents, indented by depth. Click the chevron or right-click to expand/collapse.

doc.name: useTableRowIndex — Numbered Rows
doc.description: A table with a prepended row-number column via useTableRowIndex. Numbering is monospaced, right-aligned, and follows the rows the table renders.

doc.name: useTableRowStatus - Semantic and Custom Markers
doc.description: A job table using both row-status paths: status resolves themed semantic glyphs and tones, while color stays a custom paint choice with an optional caller-selected icon or the stable dot.

doc.name: Table — Row Selection
doc.description: Table with row selection checkboxes and a select-all header checkbox.

doc.name: Table
doc.description: Data-driven table with proportional and pixel column widths and hover highlighting.

doc.name: Table — Sortable Columns
doc.description: Table with sortable columns, click headers to sort ascending or descending.

doc.name: Table — Striped Rows
doc.description: Table with alternating row colors and hover highlighting for easy scanning.

doc.name: useTableTreeData: Tree Table
doc.description: A file-tree table built from nested data. useTableTreeState flattens the tree into the visible rows and owns the expanded set; useTableTreeData draws the per-level indent and the expand/collapse chevron in the tree column. The two hooks are designed to work together, so this one example covers both. hasExpandAllControl adds the expand-all/collapse-all toggle to the tree column header. Collapsed branches are unmounted, not hidden.

doc.name: useTableColumnSettingsState — Column Visibility Picker
doc.description: A Table toolbar with a Columns menu of checkboxes: toggling Email updates active columns, Reset restores defaults, and the config is passed directly to useTableColumnSettings.

doc.name: useTableSortableState — Multi-Sort Orders
doc.description: Orders with no sort code of their own: useTableSortableState owns the sort state, returns the sorted orders, and hands useTableSortable a ready config. Click Customer, then Shift-click Total, to sort by customer and then by total within each customer. A line above the orders reads the current sort state from the hook.

doc.name: Text — Colors
doc.description: All text color options (primary, secondary, disabled, placeholder, active) applied to body text to show their intended use.

doc.name: Text — Heading Levels
doc.description: All 6 heading levels (h1 through h6) rendered with Heading to show the full type scale.

doc.name: Text — Inline
doc.description: Mixing body and code text inline within a single line using the default inline display mode.

doc.name: Text — Truncation
doc.description: Single-line and multi-line text truncation with ellipsis using maxLines in a width-constrained container.

doc.name: Text — Types
doc.description: All 5 semantic text types (body, large, label, supporting, code) with their default styling from the theme.

doc.name: Text — Weight
doc.description: The 4 font weight variants (normal, medium, semibold, bold) applied to body text.

doc.name: Text — Word Break
doc.description: Compares break-word and break-all word break modes on a long unbreakable string.

doc.name: Text — Wrap
doc.description: The 4 text-wrap modes (wrap, nowrap, balance, pretty) shown in width-constrained containers.

doc.name: TextArea — Character Count
doc.description: Textareas with maxLength and a live character counter. The counter turns red when the limit is exceeded.

doc.name: TextArea
doc.description: A text area with placeholder text.

doc.name: TextArea — States
doc.description: Required, disabled, and loading textareas side by side. Shows the interactive states the component supports.

doc.name: TextArea — Validation
doc.description: All three status variants (error, warning, and success) with status messages, plus error without a message. Use to show inline validation feedback as the user types.

doc.name: TextArea — Icon
doc.description: Textareas with a leading icon that hints at the expected content, like a chat bubble for messages or a pencil for notes.

doc.name: TextInput — Icon
doc.description: Inputs with a leading icon that hints at the expected content. Use when the icon helps users identify the field faster, like a lock for passwords or an envelope for email.

doc.name: TextInput — Search
doc.description: Search input with a hidden label, start icon, and clear button. Use for toolbar and header search bars where the icon provides sufficient context.

doc.name: TextInput — Sizes
doc.description: Small, medium, and large inputs side by side. Use small in dense UIs like table filters, medium for most forms, and large for prominent single-field pages.

doc.name: TextInput — States
doc.description: Error, warning, and success validation states with status messages. Use to show users what went wrong and how to fix it.

doc.name: TextInput — Status variant
doc.description: The statusVariant prop controls whether the status message is attached to the bordered input (default, overlapping directly below) or detached from it (floating below as a separate element with spacing).

doc.name: TextInput — Types
doc.description: Text, password, and email types plus field-level features: tooltip, required, optional, description, disabled, and loading.

doc.name: Theme — Apply Theme
doc.description: Wrap a subtree in Theme to apply a theme to every child component in that region.

doc.name: Theme — Nested Theme
doc.description: Nested Theme providers let a local region use a different theme without affecting the rest of the page.

doc.name: Theme — Distinct Themes
doc.description: Two visually distinct theme providers wrapping identical content to show how Theme changes the visual treatment of child components.

doc.name: Theme — Switch Themes
doc.description: Use state to switch the theme object passed to Theme and preview a different visual treatment.

doc.name: useTheme — Token Values
doc.description: Read resolved theme token values with useTheme for non-CSS consumers like SVG charts.

doc.name: Thumbnail — Disabled
doc.description: Thumbnails in the disabled state with reduced opacity. The open and remove buttons stay focusable and announced as disabled, and call nothing.

doc.name: Thumbnail — Gallery
doc.description: A row of clickable thumbnails with labels that open a detail view. Use for image attachment lists where users need to preview and manage uploads.

doc.name: Thumbnail — Removable
doc.description: Thumbnails with a remove button overlay. The close button uses APCA luminance detection to stay visible on both dark and light images.

doc.name: Thumbnail
doc.description: A thumbnail with an image and label.

doc.name: Thumbnail — States
doc.description: All visual states side by side: image loaded, placeholder, skeleton loading, and upload overlay. Demonstrates the full lifecycle of a thumbnail from empty to loaded.

doc.name: TimeInput — Constrained
doc.description: Time inputs with min/max constraints limiting selection to specific windows. Use to prevent out-of-bounds selections for appointments, reservations, or shift scheduling.

doc.name: TimeInput — Formats
doc.description: 12-hour, 24-hour, and seconds formats side by side. Use 12h for US-centric UIs, 24h for international or technical contexts, and seconds for precise timing.

doc.name: TimeInput — Increment
doc.description: Time input with a custom step increment. Arrow keys jump by the specified interval (e.g. 15 minutes) for quick slot-based scheduling.

doc.name: TimeInput
doc.description: A time input that uses the browser/OS picker on touch by default and Astryx typed entry on fine pointers.

doc.name: TimeInput — States
doc.description: Default, disabled, error, warning, and success states. Use status messages to give users clear feedback about their time selection.

doc.name: Timer — Formats
doc.description: Elapsed compact units and stopwatch clock notation shown from the same start time.

doc.name: Timer — Inline
doc.description: A Timer composed into status copy while inheriting the surrounding typography.

doc.name: Timer — Typography
doc.description: Timer using its Timestamp-matched default typography and an emphasized override.

doc.name: Timestamp — Auto
doc.description: Auto format that shows relative time for recent dates and switches to the full date for older ones. The default choice for most use cases.

doc.name: Timestamp — Colors
doc.description: Timestamp rendered in each available color variant: primary, secondary, disabled, and active.

doc.name: Timestamp — Formats
doc.description: All display formats side by side: date, date_time, time, and their system equivalents. Use date and date_time for user-facing UI, system variants for logs and dev tools.

doc.name: Timestamp — Relative
doc.description: Relative time labels from seconds to months ago, with hover tooltips showing the full date. Use in feeds, comment threads, and activity logs.

doc.name: Timestamp — Timezone
doc.description: Timestamps with the timezone abbreviation appended. Enable isTimezoneShown for audiences across time zones, like audit logs or team calendars.

doc.name: Timestamp — Tooltip time zones
doc.description: Hover tooltips that show one instant across several time zones or formats. Use tooltipEntries when readers must compare zones, like an incident log carrying both the reader's time and the event's origin zone.

doc.name: Toast — Action
doc.description: Persistent toasts with a trailing button or link so the user can act on the notification, like undoing a delete or viewing a report.

doc.name: Toast — Deduplication
doc.description: Prevent duplicate toasts with uniqueID. Use ignore to keep the first toast, or overwrite to replace it with updated content like a progress percentage.

doc.name: Toast — Dismiss
doc.description: Show a persistent toast and dismiss it programmatically using the function returned by useToast. Use for long-running operations that need manual cleanup.

doc.name: Toast
doc.description: Imperative toast notifications triggered with useToast and rendered in the toast viewport.

doc.name: Toast — Stacking
doc.description: Multiple toasts stacking vertically with smooth enter and exit animations. Click repeatedly to see how toasts queue and dismiss.

doc.name: Toast — Types
doc.description: Info and error toast variants side by side. Info toasts auto-dismiss after 5 seconds, error toasts persist until the user dismisses them.

doc.name: useToast — Settings Saved
doc.description: Shows a toast from the function useToast returns: a "Settings saved" confirmation with an Undo action, a uniqueID so pressing the button again replaces the toast instead of stacking another, and an error toast when the request fails.

doc.name: ToggleButton — Color
doc.description: Toggle buttons with colored icons in the pressed state. Shows accent-colored toolbar formatting and semantic reaction colors (yellow star, red heart, blue bookmark).

doc.name: ToggleButton — Group
doc.description: Toggle button groups in single-select and multi-select modes. Single selection acts as a view mode switcher; multiple selection forms a formatting toolbar.

doc.name: ToggleButton — Icon Swap
doc.description: Icon-only toggle buttons that swap between outline and solid icons when pressed. Use for actions like favorite, bookmark, or mute where the icon itself communicates the state.

doc.name: ToggleButton — Label
doc.description: Toggle buttons with visible text labels that show a font weight shift on press. Use when the icon alone is not enough to communicate the action.

doc.name: ToggleButton — States
doc.description: Default, pressed, disabled, and loading states of a standalone toggle button. Shows how visual treatment changes across states.

doc.name: ToggleButtonGroup
doc.description: ToggleButtonGroup manages a set of ToggleButtons with single-select or multi-select behavior for options like view modes or filters.

doc.name: ToggleButtonGroup — Vertical
doc.description: A vertically stacked ToggleButtonGroup using the vertical orientation, shown with both single-select and multi-select behavior, ideal for sidebar-style option lists and vertical toolbars.

doc.name: Token — Clickable
doc.description: Interactive tokens that respond to clicks. Use for toggleable filters or tokens that open a detail view when selected.

doc.name: Token — Colors
doc.description: All 11 color variants in default and disabled states. Use color to categorize entities or convey status at a glance.

doc.name: Token — End Content
doc.description: Tokens with trailing content like a count badge or status indicator after the label. Use for notification counts, item quantities, or compact status info.

doc.name: Token — Icon
doc.description: Tokens with a leading icon that identifies the entity type. Use when the icon helps users recognize the token category faster, like a user icon for people or a tag icon for labels.

doc.name: Token — Removable
doc.description: Tokens with a dismiss button for selections the user can undo. Use in multi-select fields, active filters, or any list of user-chosen items.

doc.name: Tokenizer — Clear
doc.description: Tokenizer with a built-in clear-all button for bulk removal of all selected tokens. On touch screens, clear through the sheet's Clear all.

doc.name: Tokenizer — Creatable
doc.description: Free-text tokenizer for creating custom tags and a combined create-or-search pattern. Use when users need to enter values that may not exist in a predefined list.

doc.name: Tokenizer — End Content
doc.description: Tokenizer with an action button in the end slot. Use for inline actions like applying selections alongside the input.

doc.name: Tokenizer — Icon
doc.description: Tokenizer with a leading search icon to visually reinforce the search behavior.

doc.name: Tokenizer — Max Entries
doc.description: Tokenizer with a maximum selection limit. The input hides automatically when the limit is reached, preventing further additions.

doc.name: Tokenizer — Overflow
doc.description: Tokenizer with overflow truncation when unfocused. Inline mode pushes content down on expand; layer mode overlays without shifting layout. Overflow modes apply to the inline field.

doc.name: Tokenizer
doc.description: A tokenizer with preset tags and search source.

doc.name: Tokenizer — States
doc.description: Tokenizer in disabled, error, warning, and success states. Use to communicate validation feedback or lock a selection from editing.

doc.name: Toolbar — Bulk Actions
doc.description: A compact toolbar with the muted variant for showing bulk selection actions. Use when the user selects multiple items in a list or table and needs quick access to batch operations.

doc.name: Toolbar — Card Header
doc.description: A toolbar as a card header with a left-aligned title and icon actions on the right. Use Toolbar instead of LayoutHeader when your card header has interactive actions; Toolbar adds start/end slot layout, keyboard navigation, and automatic size cascading. If the header is just a title with no actions, a LayoutHeader or Section is enough.

doc.name: Toolbar — Sizes
doc.description: Small, medium, and large toolbars side by side. The size prop cascades to child buttons and inputs automatically. Use small in dense UIs like cards, medium for most cases, and large for spacious layouts.

doc.name: Toolbar — Table Filter
doc.description: Filter bar above a table: a search box leads the row, each field beside it is a closed trigger that doubles as its own filter chip — the bare field name unset, the whole clause once set — and the clauses fold from the end into a count as the row narrows, followed by a live result count, a clear all, and a column picker. Use to search, filter, and narrow flat rows of records such as jobs, orders, tickets, or users.

doc.name: Toolbar — Three Slot
doc.description: A toolbar with start, center, and end content using the three-column grid layout. Use when you need a centered title or heading with navigation and actions on either side.

doc.name: Toolbar — Tab Navigation
doc.description: A toolbar with tabs in the start slot and an action button at the end. Use as a card or section header when content is split into tabs with a primary action alongside.

doc.name: Tooltip — Action Bar
doc.description: Tooltips on an action button bar with contextual descriptions.

doc.name: Tooltip — Hook Usage
doc.description: Tooltip using the useTooltip hook for programmatic control.

doc.name: Tooltip — Inline Text
doc.description: Tooltips on inline text terms for definitions.

doc.name: TopNav — Centered Navigation
doc.description: Navigation layout with center-aligned nav items flanked by a logo heading and end actions.

doc.name: TopNav — Enterprise Dashboard
doc.description: Full-featured navigation bar with icon-labeled nav items, search, notifications, and a primary CTA.

doc.name: TopNav — Hover Menu
doc.description: Navigation bar with a hover-triggered dropdown menu showing product items with icons and descriptions.

doc.name: TopNav — Mega Menu
doc.description: Marketing-style navigation with a full-width mega menu featuring product items and a promotional featured card.

doc.name: TopNav — Multiple Dropdowns
doc.description: Navigation bar with multiple hover-triggered dropdown menus that auto-close when switching between them.

doc.name: TopNav — With Logo
doc.description: Navigation bar with a branded logo icon, heading link, nav items, and a profile action.

doc.name: TopNavHeading — Basic
doc.description: A product heading with a logo inside a TopNav, linked to the home page. Use as the leading brand element of a top navigation bar.

doc.name: TopNavHeading
doc.description: Demonstrates TopNavHeading with a logo and text, both as a plain display and as a clickable link.

doc.name: TopNavItem — Basic
doc.description: Navigation links inside a TopNav with one item marked as selected. Use for top-level pages of an application.

doc.name: TopNavItem
doc.description: Demonstrates TopNavItem with selected, icon, disabled, and default states.

doc.name: TopNavMegaMenu — Basic
doc.description: A mega menu trigger inside a TopNav that opens a panel of rich link items. Use when a navigation section has multiple destinations worth describing.

doc.name: TopNavMegaMenu
doc.description: Demonstrates TopNavMegaMenu with items and a featured card in the mega menu panel.

doc.name: TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard — Basic
doc.description: A promotional card with a title, description, and call-to-action link. Pass it to the featured slot of a TopNavMegaMenu to highlight announcements.

doc.name: TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard
doc.displayName: Top Nav Mega Menu Featured Card
doc.description: Demonstrates TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard with a title, description, and CTA link inside a mega menu.

doc.name: TopNavMegaMenuItem — Basic
doc.description: Rich link items with an icon, title, and description. Use inside the items slot of a TopNavMegaMenu to describe each destination.

doc.name: TopNavMegaMenuItem
doc.description: Demonstrates TopNavMegaMenuItem with icons, titles, and descriptions inside a mega menu.

doc.name: TopNavMenu — Basic
doc.description: A dropdown menu inside a TopNav built from an items array with icons and descriptions. Use to group related destinations under a single trigger.

doc.name: TopNavMenu
doc.description: Demonstrates TopNavMenu with a hover-triggered dropdown containing items with icons and descriptions.

doc.name: TreeList — File Tree With Icons
doc.description: File browser tree with folder and document icons distinguishing directories from files.

doc.name: TreeList — Interactive Settings
doc.description: Settings tree with clickable items and a documentation link.

doc.name: TreeList — Mailbox Tree

doc.name: TreeList — Navigation Tree
doc.description: Navigation tree with a selected item for the current page.

doc.name: Typeahead — Limited Results
doc.description: Typeahead with a capped dropdown showing at most three results.

doc.name: Typeahead — Search Field
doc.description: Search input with icon and suggestions on focus.

doc.name: Typeahead — With Helper Text
doc.description: Typeahead with a description below the label.

doc.name: Typeahead — With Validation
doc.description: Typeahead with an error validation message.
