doc.description: Typeahead with custom item rendering using TypeaheadItem for avatars and descriptions.

doc.name: VStack — Basic
doc.description: A heading and paragraphs stacked vertically with a consistent gap. Use VStack whenever siblings should flow top to bottom with even spacing.

doc.name: VStack
doc.description: Demonstrates VStack arranging items vertically with different gaps.

doc.name: VisuallyHidden — Live Region
doc.description: A polite aria-live region announces visual-only state changes to assistive technology.

doc.name: VisuallyHidden — Structural Heading
doc.description: Give a visually implicit section an accessible name so screen-reader users can navigate to it.

doc.name: VisuallyHidden — Supplementary Context
doc.description: Stat cards whose trend arrows get screen-reader-only text, so a change like +12% is read as an increase from last month. Use to make terse visual data accessible.

doc.name: createAnimator — Playing cards in plain JavaScript
doc.displayName: createAnimator — Playing cards in plain JavaScript
doc.description: The playing card from the useAnimator example, built in plain JavaScript with createAnimator and pointer events: it follows a drag, springs back on a gentle release, flies off with momentum on a quick flick, and a button discards it from the keyboard. React only mounts it.

doc.name: createDragToSnapPoints — Playing card in plain JavaScript
doc.displayName: createDragToSnapPoints — Playing card in plain JavaScript
doc.description: The three-place playing card from the useDragToSnapPoints example, built in plain JavaScript with createDragToSnapPoints: a sideways drag settles it on the nearest place or the next after a flick, buttons settle it from the keyboard, and a live region announces the place. React only mounts it.

doc.name: useAnimator — Playing cards
doc.description: A playing card that follows a drag: a gentle release springs it back on its release velocity, and a quick flick throws it away with momentum before the next card is dealt. A Discard button moves it off from the keyboard, fading it in place under Reduce Motion, and the discard is announced. Built only on the public useAnimator hook.

doc.name: useDragToSnapPoints — Playing card on three places
doc.displayName: useDragToSnapPoints — Playing card on three places
doc.description: A playing card that a sideways drag moves between three places: a slow release settles on the nearest, a quick flick carries to the next, and a release moving back returns where it started. Buttons settle it from the keyboard, and the new place is announced. Built only on the public useDragToSnapPoints hook.

doc.name: usePanGesture — A draggable box
doc.description: The smallest pan example, in two forms side by side: the usePanGesture hook and the createPanGesture factory. The factory takes any element, React or not. Each card names its API, follows a drag from a finger, a mouse or a pen, and springs back, with the same StyleX styles. A starting point for a draggable tile, a swipe or any drag-and-release gesture.

doc.name: usePanGesture — A playing card (advanced)
doc.description: An advanced usePanGesture example: a playing card follows a drag, settles back on a gentle release and flies off on a quick flick, while a Discard button deals the next card from the keyboard and announces it. Drag, settle and throw are StyleX styles driven by React state. A pattern for swipe-to-dismiss, card decks and flick gestures.

doc.name: AI Chat Landing
doc.description: Zero-state entry surface centered on a single composer with suggestion chips instead of history, sized for the moment before any content exists. The empty counterpart to a transcript.

doc.name: AI Chat Conversation
doc.description: Transcript of alternating turns carrying mixed rich content inline (markdown, code blocks, collapsible tool-call output) beside a resizable artifact panel that holds generated output while the stream keeps scrolling.

doc.name: Blank
doc.description: Bare scaffold: one heading slot, one empty content region, no navigation and no chrome. The starting point when every other layout imposes more structure than wanted.

doc.name: Canvas Editor
doc.description: Layered artboard workspace: document tabs over a layer rail, a fixed-size frame you zoom on a muted backdrop, and an inspector of position, type, and filter fields that retargets to the selected layer. Objects hold a coordinate rather than reflowing, so moving one never moves another.

doc.name: Centered Hero
doc.description: Symmetrical centered stack (headline, short blurb, paired call-to-action buttons) resting on one wide full-bleed picture, with nothing on either flank competing.

doc.name: Checkout Wizard
doc.description: Multi-step checkout, cart, order, and payment wizard with a running summary that recalculates as answers change. It adapts to its host width, renders the summary first on narrow surfaces, validates every forward path, and completes locally without sending payment.

doc.name: Classic Gallery
doc.description: Uniform grid of equal-ratio media tiles under a centered intro, with filter tabs that narrow the set in place. Regular rhythm, unlike the variable-height masonry variant.

doc.name: Contact Form
doc.description: Flat single-column form mixing control types (text, pill toggles, dropdowns, long free-text) landing on one full-width submit. No steps, no branching, no summary rail.

doc.name: Course Detail
doc.description: Long-form sales page for a single offering, in two columns — read the pitch, then enroll from a sticky rail. The main column holds a preview poster with a fact row, an about block with skill chips, a module syllabus whose sections collapse module by module, an instructor card, reviews with a scored-aspects panel, and a FAQ; the rail holds the price, a self-paced or cohort start picker, and a weekly-pace slider that computes a finish date. The shape for any offering with a curriculum and a purchase panel — a course, class, masterclass, bootcamp, workshop, or training.

doc.name: Service Monitoring Dashboard
doc.description: Always-on analytics with a triage rail: status-colored tiles with sparklines, multi-series time charts over a switchable window, and an independently scrolling alert column that folds into the content when narrow.

doc.name: Funnel & Cohort Dashboard
doc.description: Analytics for sequence and retention questions, pairing two shapes a plain dashboard cannot hold: a staged funnel where each step reads as drop-off against the one before, and a two-axis cohort matrix rendered as a heatmap.

doc.name: Data Dashboard
doc.description: Comparison-heavy analytics behind a persistent filter bar: tiles that each carry an inline sparkline and several period-over-period deltas, then segmented breakdowns underneath. Every number is shown against another number.

doc.name: Portfolio Dashboard
doc.description: Analytics for a value-over-time question: balance and change tiles above a stacked area chart of composition through time, closing on a ranked table of the largest contributors.

doc.name: Project Status Dashboard
doc.description: Status analytics mixing progress and time-axis shapes: a completion donut, a horizontal timeline of dated bars against a today marker, a per-owner table with progress and status, an at-risk list, and a burndown.

doc.name: Executive Summary Dashboard
doc.description: Report-shaped analytics with a prose rail beside the charts: a scorecard of headline numbers with period deltas and status coloring, goal-attainment bars, a trend grid, and a written commentary column that folds beneath the content when narrow.

doc.name: Analytics Dashboard
doc.description: Three-band analytics: a row of headline tiles, then charts, then supporting tables, all re-reading from one global filter bar. Breadth over depth, a summary surface rather than a drill-down.

doc.name: Order Detail
doc.description: Single-record detail in two columns: a summary header with status and actions, a repeating line-item list, a totals block that sums it, and a chronological activity timeline in the rail. The shape for any record holding children plus a history: a customer order with shipping, an invoice, a transaction, or a job.

doc.name: Documentation Design
doc.description: Reference article alternating prose with live rendered examples: an interactive preview, a property table, paired do and don't comparisons, and copyable code blocks.

doc.name: Documentation Technical
doc.description: Reference article ordered as sequential numbered steps with code at each stage, plus callout cards for prerequisites and onward links. A linear walkthrough rather than a browsable reference.

doc.name: Documentation Catalog
doc.description: Reference landing that is pure wayfinding: a banner above a grid of category cards linking into sections, with no article content on the surface itself.

doc.name: Page Editor
doc.description: Three-pane authoring workspace: a source palette on one flank, a live canvas in the middle, and an inspector that retargets to whatever is selected. Drag and drop to reorder, edit to see it render immediately.

doc.name: File Explorer
doc.description: Hierarchical browser that drills through nested levels as adjacent columns rather than replacing the list each time, with breadcrumb history, switchable list and grid density, and a metadata pane for the selected node.

doc.name: Two-column Form
doc.description: Form split into two columns beneath a hero header: inputs on one flank, a persistent context panel opposite that stays put while the fields scroll. Flat, single submit, no steps.

doc.name: Dialog Wizard
doc.description: Step through a short flow in a dialog, overlay, or popup launched from the page underneath, which stays where it was. Compact step markers and a pinned action row inside a constrained width, rather than the full page a wizard usually gets. Best for two to four short steps — setup, invite, schedule, onboarding — where losing the context underneath would cost more than the flow is worth.

doc.name: Inline Wizard
doc.description: Accordion wizard stacking every step in one column: the active step expands in place while finished ones collapse to a single line carrying their result and a way back in. Steps that run themselves expand into a nested stepper that ticks check by check and halts the column where one fails. Best when later steps depend on what earlier ones decided.

doc.name: Vertical Wizard
doc.description: Multi-step wizard with the steps in a fixed left rail that stays visible while the form scrolls, plus a side panel whose guidance follows the focused field. Suits long or unequal steps carrying uploads, previews, and dense review metadata. As width tightens the guidance drops first, then the rail rotates into a horizontal stepper above the form.

doc.name: Form Wizard
doc.description: Linear multi-step form that moves through one panel at a time, with a horizontal progress track pinned above rather than running down a rail, so every step keeps the full content width for its fields. Only the current step renders, unlike an accordion where each section expands into one long scrolling form. Each advance is validated, and a step left broken stays flagged to jump back to.

doc.name: Gallery Hero
doc.description: Centered stack (headline, short blurb, call-to-action buttons) resolving into a multi-image photo grid rather than one wide full-bleed picture, so the imagery reads as a set.

doc.name: IDE
doc.description: Dense multi-pane workspace of resizable, collapsible regions: a hierarchy tree on one flank, tabbed documents in the middle, a docked drawer along the bottom, an inspector opposite. Drag a divider to resize or collapse any of them.

doc.name: Incident Console
doc.description: Dense row queue with an inspector: severity-coded rows grouped by status, a saved-search filter bar, a segmented status control, and a resizable detail pane for the selected row. Rows, not cards, sized for scanning volume.

doc.name: Kanban Board
doc.description: Horizontal lanes of draggable cards where the column itself is the status, so drag and drop between lanes is the state change. Fixed columns, variable-height cards.

doc.name: Card Grid
doc.description: Searchable, browsable card grid with filter tabs and a real empty state: uniform tiles organized by topic, narrowing in place, with no detail surface behind them.

doc.name: Login Card
doc.description: Credential form inside an elevated centered card, third-party provider buttons separated from the fields by a divider, secondary sign-up and legal links beneath.

doc.name: Login Split
doc.description: Credential form filling one half of a two-pane split, full-bleed media holding the other. Same fields as the card variant, but the layout carries brand imagery.

doc.name: Login SSO
doc.description: Progressive credential flow that branches on input: the email domain resolves an identity provider and redirects, with a password path as fallback. Two-stage rather than one form.

doc.name: Basic Login
doc.description: Minimal centered credential form on a plain ground: two fields and a submit, nothing competing for attention. The least-chrome entry surface.

doc.name: Messaging Shell
doc.description: Four-column nested navigation narrowing left to right (team workspace, channel list, message stream, thread panel) where each column scopes the next. Dense rows, zero cards.

doc.name: Mixed Gallery
doc.description: Masonry grid of variable-height tiles that pack against each other instead of cropping to a shared ratio, captioned per tile. Irregular rhythm, unlike the uniform gallery.

doc.name: Checkout Form
doc.description: Long sectioned form running beside a summary that stays visible while the fields scroll and recalculates as they change, ending on a terminal confirm of the total. Sections run contact, address, delivery choice, then card details.

doc.name: Product Detail
doc.description: Single-item detail pairing a media gallery with a selection column: variant swatches, a quantity stepper, primary and secondary commit actions, and collapsible specification sections below.

doc.name: Product Gallery
doc.description: Uniform card grid where every tile carries media, title, supporting line, and a price. Browse-to-select only, with no filtering and no detail surface.

doc.name: Settings Dialog
doc.description: Preferences inside a modal container with searchable section navigation, so configuration happens without leaving whatever is underneath. Grouped toggles, live preview of appearance choices, rebindable shortcuts.

doc.name: Settings Panels
doc.description: Preferences split into nav-switched panels: a persistent section list swaps the pane beside it, and rows edit in place rather than opening a separate form.

doc.name: Settings Form
doc.description: Preferences as one continuously scrolling form, sections stacked in order with no navigation between them. The simplest settings shape: everything reachable by scrolling.

doc.name: Shell Nav
doc.description: Application frame combining both navigation axes: a top menu bar with command-palette search over a resizable hierarchy rail, wrapping placeholder content. For when one axis is not enough.

doc.name: Side Nav
doc.description: Application frame with a single collapsible, resizable left rail carrying grouped history and search, wrapping the main content. Vertical navigation only, no top bar.

doc.name: Top Nav
doc.description: Application frame with horizontal navigation only: a centered bar whose items open full-width mega-menu panels, over placeholder content that keeps the entire width.

doc.name: Side Gallery
doc.description: Asymmetric split section: a copy column of headline, supporting text, and links held against a clustered image collage opposite. Deliberately off-balance, unlike the centered hero.

doc.name: Collapsible Table
doc.description: Several tables on one page, each in a collapsible card with its own columns — for groups that do not share a schema, where one table would stand full of empty cells. One time range drives them all, and rows expand into a history chart. Accounts, integrations, sections, sort, expand, or collapse.

doc.name: Comparison Table
doc.description: Transposed matrix that puts candidates in the columns and criteria in grouped rows, with a pinned label column that survives horizontal scroll, columns you can swap or add, and best-in-row marks you can toggle. Compare, comparison, matrix, spec sheet, feature grid, pricing table, benchmark, frozen column, sticky column, or side-by-side.

doc.name: Filterable Table
doc.description: Flat row collection built around progressive filtering: a token bar that escalates into full query syntax, saved views that persist a filter set, column and grouping options, and a resizable detail pane.

doc.name: Grouped Table
doc.description: Row collection bundled into collapsible sections with per-group counts, so a long list reads as a handful of blocks that expand and collapse. Query filtering and a resizable inspector for the selected row.

doc.name: Inbox Table
doc.description: Two-pane message queue: the table indexes a reading pane rather than being the destination, with a divider you drag to resize. Rows stack when the table narrows, not the window; threads read as collapsible messages; replying opens a composer that leaves the list live.

doc.name: Searchable Table
doc.description: Flat table of uniform rows under a block of record-level facts, narrowed three ways at once — a full-text search box, a scope toggle, and per-column popovers — with sortable and filterable columns, per-row hover detail, and totals derived from the visible rows that flag themselves as partial while a filter is on. The shape for one homogeneous list, not nested rows or groups with their own columns.

doc.name: Tree Table
doc.description: Hierarchical table where every parent row rolls up from its children — a code repository whose folders show the newest commit beneath them, beside a detail sidebar and a rendered README. Columns resize, siblings sort within their own level, arrow keys walk the rows, and search prunes the tree to matching branches.

doc.name: Simple Table
doc.description: Flat row collection where columns sort, rows select into a bulk-action toolbar, and each row carries an overflow menu. Sortable but ungrouped, with no detail pane, the baseline shape.

doc.name: Theme Showcase
doc.description: Multi-surface comparison shell: preview palettes, typography, icons and control states across a storefront, checkout, chat and inventory on one responsive canvas. A theme preview and design-system showcase, with an embeddable content view for an existing app shell.

doc.name: Work Item Detail
doc.description: Single work-item detail in two columns: a title with a status selector, a description, a subtask checklist with progress, an attachments block, and a comment and activity feed in the main column, plus a property rail with assignee, dates, labels, and linked items. The shape for any tracked item with children, properties, and a comment history — a task, ticket, issue, story, bug, card, request, or work item.

default.description: Warm chocolate theme for Astryx — rich brown palette with Fraunces headings, Albert Sans body, and Lucide icons

default.name: neutral
default.description: Restrained warm grays. Minimal and quiet, so the content stays the focus.

default.description: Warm stone and slate, earthy and understated, with just enough character to feel handcrafted.

default.name: y2k
default.description: Hot pinks, lime greens, and Poppins. Bubbly, playful, and unmistakably retro.

doc.name: codemod
doc.description: A codemod module the CLI runs during `{@command upgrade}`. Default-export a plain object with a `type` discriminant: 'code' rewrites source files, 'config' rewrites the astryx.config.* file. There is no factory to call.
doc.appliesTo: `<codemods>/<version>/<id>.{ts,mjs,js}` in an integration package: `<codemods>` is the codemods root of astryx.integration.*, and `<version>` is the exact @astryxdesign/core version (such as 0.7.0) whose upgrade runs the codemod. A file directly in the root never runs.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Short, human-readable title shown in upgrade output.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional longer description.

fields.name: isOptional
fields.description: When true, the codemod runs only when explicitly requested.

fields.name: fileExtensions
fields.description: File extensions this codemod applies to. Code codemods only; a config codemod always targets astryx.config.*.

fields.name: transform
fields.type: (file: AstryxCodemodFile, api: AstryxCodemodApi) => string | null | undefined
fields.description: The transform. Return the new source to rewrite the file, or null/undefined to leave it unchanged.

fields.name: file
fields.description: The source file presented to the transform.

fields.name: file.path
fields.description: Absolute path to the file being transformed.

fields.name: file.source
fields.description: The current source contents of the file.

fields.name: api
fields.description: Helpers and context passed as the second argument.

fields.name: api.jscodeshift
fields.description: A jscodeshift instance configured with a parser for the file.

fields.name: api.stats
fields.description: Accepted for jscodeshift parity. A call does nothing, and upgrade shows nothing for it.

fields.name: api.report
fields.description: Accepted for jscodeshift parity. A call does nothing, and upgrade shows nothing for it.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Discriminant for the file-transforming variant. Use 'config' for a codemod that rewrites astryx.config.* instead (see notes).

examples.label: Code codemod (type: code)
Config codemod (type: config)

notes.text: The config-codemod variant (type: 'config') carries the same fields as a code codemod except fileExtensions: it always targets the astryx.config.* file rather than a set of source files.

Authors write a plain object and default-export it with the `type` discriminant; there is no factory. The CLI validates it at the load boundary via parseCodemod with a strict schema, and isOptional defaults to false.

doc.name: config
doc.description: The optional astryx.config.* file at your project root. Declares which integrations to load, where to route issue links, post-codemod hooks, local debug-log and gap-report handlers, a discover source, and experimental layout components. All optional; {} is valid.

fields.name: integrations
fields.description: Package names of Astryx integrations to load alongside core.

fields.name: issuesUrl
fields.description: Where reports about Core go: `{@command gap-report}` routes a Core report here when no handler is loaded, gapReport handlers receive it as `report.target.issuesUrl`, and `{@command swizzle}` prints it as the feedback link for a Core component. A report or swizzle for an integration's component uses that integration's own issuesUrl, never this one. An absolute URL; a value that is not a URL makes the config invalid.

fields.name: hooks
fields.description: Lifecycle hooks.

fields.name: hooks.postCodemod
fields.description: Commands to run after `{@command upgrade}` changes files (e.g. re-run your formatter). Each hook is an object `{name?, buildCommand}`: buildCommand gets `{packageDir, files}` and returns `{command, args?, options?}` to run, or null to skip. A dry run prints each command instead of running it.

fields.name: debug
fields.description: Record every command run. The handler is synchronous; promises are not awaited and output goes to stderr. Declare `debug` directly in this file so early commands can discover it. An integration can supply one too, as a `debug` named export from its manifest. Every handler runs: yours first, then each integration's in load order (the `integrations` list, then autolinked ones). A handler that throws is skipped; the others still run and the command's result does not change. Set `{"astryx": {"inheritDebug": false}}` in package.json to take only your own.

fields.name: gapReport
fields.description: Handle explicit gap reports in addition to every loaded integration handler. The project handler runs first. Public handlers require caller consent; internal handlers always run.

fields.name: discover
fields.description: Tell `{@command discover}` which integrations this project could add: an async function that returns a catalog. An integration can provide one too, as a `discover` named export from its manifest. Discover calls every source, yours first, and one that fails never hides the others. Discover only reads; your package manager installs.
fields.example: async ({signal, package: name, version}) => fetchCatalog({signal, name, version})

fields.name: experimental
fields.description: Unstable features; may change without a breaking bump.

fields.name: experimental.iconSet
fields.description: Experimental: may change or be removed in a patch release. The project's icon set, by set name or as `<package>/<set>`. It is the opt-in: copied templates use its icons, and `astryx discover` and `astryx doctor` report icon sets, only when it is set. `astryx experimental icon` ranks its icons first; without it, the only installed set is the project's there. `astryx search` never returns icons.

fields.name: experimental.xle.components
fields.description: Custom components for the removed layout expander, keyed by component name. The CLI still validates the field, so an entry without a string `from` makes `astryx.config` invalid, but nothing reads it.

examples.label: Send every command run somewhere of your own

notes.text: The config is validated at load with a strict schema: an unknown key, a misspelled one included, or a value of the wrong type makes the whole file invalid. `{@command gap-report}`, `{@command discover}`, and `{@command upgrade}` stop with the error, and `{@command doctor}` fails its `config` check (exit 1). Reads such as `component`, `docs`, `search`, `template`, and `theme` carry on silently as if there were no config and no integrations, and no debug handler runs, so run `{@command doctor}` after editing the file.

doc.name: debug-event
doc.description: One recorded CLI run: what a `debug` handler receives, whether it is set in astryx.config or exported by an integration manifest. There is exactly one event per run, and every field is present by the time a handler sees it.

fields.name: schemaVersion
fields.description: Version of the recorded shape: 1, 2, or 3. A field that changes meaning gets a new version, so switch on this.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Unique per run. Deduplicate on it.

fields.name: startedAt
fields.description: When the run started, as ISO 8601.

fields.name: endedAt
fields.description: When the run ended, as ISO 8601.

fields.name: durationMs
fields.description: How long the run took, in milliseconds.

fields.name: command
fields.description: The full command name. Empty when astryx ran without a command.

fields.name: commandPath
fields.description: The command name split into segments.

fields.name: argv
fields.description: The arguments after the binary, scrubbed.

fields.name: args
fields.description: Positional arguments, keyed by their declared names.

fields.name: options
fields.description: The command options, as the CLI resolved them.

fields.name: optionSources
fields.description: Where each option value came from: 'cli', 'default', 'env', 'config', or 'implied'. The keys match `options`.

fields.name: globalOptions
fields.description: The root flags, such as --json, --detail, and --lang.

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: How the run ended: 'ok', 'error', 'parse-error', 'fatal', 'rejected', or 'incomplete'.

fields.name: exitCode
fields.description: The process exit code. When a signal ended the run, 128 plus the signal number.

fields.name: signal
fields.description: The signal that ended the run, such as 'SIGINT'. Null otherwise.

fields.name: error
fields.description: The failure: `name`, `message`, `code`, and `stack`. Branch on `code`, never on `message`. Null when nothing failed.

fields.name: output
fields.description: What the run answered with: JSON mode, the envelope types, the result count and kind, and the stdout and stderr it printed, scrubbed and cut at the capture limit.

fields.name: env
fields.description: Runtime facts: the CLI and Node versions, platform, CI, package manager, and whether a person, an AI agent, or automation ran the command. It never holds a hostname, a user name, or a raw session ID.

fields.name: project
fields.description: The project the command ran in, as flags and counts. It never holds package names.

fields.name: redacted
fields.description: Whether the values in the record were scrubbed. It is true on every event a handler receives. When it is false, treat the log as sensitive.

examples.label: Keep a local log of the runs that failed

notes.text: The shape only grows: fields are added, never removed or given a new meaning. When a meaning must change, `schemaVersion` gets a new value. In version 3, a null `output.resultKind` means the run never reached an answer, so do not count it together with a version 1 or 2 null.
The handler runs synchronously as the process exits, so a promise it returns is never awaited. It gets a copy of the event, and anything it throws is ignored.
Import DebugEventOutput, DebugEventEnv, DebugEventProject, and DebugEventError from @astryxdesign/cli/authoring for the fields of `output`, `env`, `project`, and `error`.

doc.name: discover-source
doc.description: A source for `{@command discover}`: an async function that returns a catalog of packages a project could add, their versions, and what each version adds. Set it as `discover` in astryx.config, or export it as `discover` from an integration manifest. Discover calls every source, the project one first, and then reads the official list the CLI carries; another source's entry for an official package is kept. A source that throws, runs past 30 seconds, or returns an invalid catalog never hides the others; discover then uses the last good answer that source gave for the same request, or reports the source as failed when it saved none. Discover only reads: it prints the command that adds a package and never runs it.
doc.appliesTo: `discover` in astryx.config.*, or the `discover` named export of astryx.integration.*

fields.name: context
fields.description: The one argument the source is called with.

fields.name: context.signal
fields.description: Aborted when the source runs past 30 seconds.

fields.name: context.package
fields.description: Set when discover shows one package: return that package with every version.

fields.name: context.version
fields.description: With `package`: return that version's contributions. Without it, the latest release's.

fields.name: returns
fields.description: The catalog. Discover checks it, ignores fields and item kinds it does not know, and refuses any schemaVersion but 1.

fields.name: schemaVersion
fields.description: Version of the catalog shape.

fields.name: source
fields.description: Who answered, when the data was produced (ISO 8601), and false when the source knows its list is partial.

fields.name: packages
fields.description: One entry per npm package. When two sources list the same package, the earlier source wins.

fields.name: packages[].package
fields.description: The npm name.

fields.name: packages[].integration
fields.description: Shared by every npm name that publishes the same integration. Discover lists an integration once.

fields.name: packages[].aliases
fields.description: The integration's other npm names. Discover never offers a package the project has under another name.

fields.name: packages[].description
fields.description: One line, for the list and search.

fields.name: packages[].latest
fields.description: The latest release. Null when there are only prereleases.

fields.name: packages[].versions
fields.description: Every version, newest first: `{version, publishedAt, prerelease, status}`, where status is `ok` or why the version could not be read.

fields.name: packages[].contributions
fields.description: What the requested (else latest) version adds: `{kind, name, title?, summary?, keywords?}`, where kind is `component`, `template`, `doc`, `theme`, `codemod`, or `agent-doc` (a DiscoverKind) and name is the name the CLI uses for it.

examples.label: A project source in astryx.config

notes.text: In global mode: the discover source of an integration installed for the computer is called in folders outside any project; inside a project, only the sources of integrations the project installs are. See {@link namespace:global} and {@link generic:global-integrations}.

doc.name: authored-doc-graph-fields
doc.description: Fields every authored doc kind can declare for the docs tree: `placement`, `stability`, and two reserved fields, `aliases` and `audience`. The docs tree reads `placement` for every guide and namespace doc, the CLI's and each integration's. Nothing reads `aliases` or `audience` today: a reference topic that sets one fails to load, placed in the docs tree or not, and other doc kinds accept them and ignore them.
doc.appliesTo: Every authored doc kind's .doc.mjs object. Theme descriptors take none of these fields.

fields.name: placement
fields.description: Names the doc's one parent in the docs tree: a namespace of the same package, one of its slots, and an order. Read for every guide, the CLI's and each integration's, and for every namespace doc: a guide with `placement` gets a route in the tree instead of a flat topic name, and cannot also set `replaces` or `extends`; a namespace doc with `placement` nests under that parent. In the CLI's own topic directory a topic that sets it fails to load: the CLI keeps its guides in its docs tree directory. Commands, API functions, schemas, and enums do not set it: the tree adopts each by its `namespace`.

fields.name: placement.parent
fields.description: The parent namespace: `namespace:<name>` in the same package.

fields.name: placement.slot
fields.description: A slot the parent namespace declares; it must accept this doc's kind. Optional when the parent has one slot.

fields.name: placement.order
fields.description: Integer sibling order within the slot. Docs without an order come after the ordered ones, sorted by title. The same order sets each doc's Previous and Next links.

fields.name: aliases
fields.description: Reserved: prior names or routes the docs tree will keep resolving to this doc, without creating another identity. Nothing reads it today, and a topic that sets it fails to load.

fields.name: audience
fields.description: Reserved: which docs bundle includes this doc ('public' when omitted). Nothing reads it today, and a topic that sets it fails to load.

fields.name: stability
fields.description: Marks the doc of an experimental surface: one whose shape can still change, or disappear, in any patch release. A command's help shows it as `[experimental]`. The doc's own text still says so. Omit it for a stable surface.

notes.text: Unknown fields: `component`, `function`, `generic`, `schema`, `command` and `enum` docs accept a field they do not know, and nothing reads it, so a doc written for a newer CLI still loads here. `page`, `block` and `namespace` docs refuse one, as do `theme` descriptors. Sections and content blocks refuse one in every doc.

doc.name: command-doc
doc.description: The doc-type for a CLI command: the terminal binding of an operation. A command is not its own behavior; it is a FunctionDoc exposed on the CLI, referenced via `fn`, carrying only CLI-surface facts (args, flags, subcommands, examples, exit codes). A `defineCommand` converter turns it into Commander config + `--help`.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant. Marks the file as a command doc.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Command path, e.g. 'search' | 'theme build'.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Human-readable display name, e.g. 'astryx search'.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-line summary → Commander `.description()` + the docs listing.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Longer body / when-to-use. `astryx docs` prints it after the summary; `--help` shows only the summary.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: Optional in the type, but every doc the CLI ships declares it. The group that reads this doc. The CLI's commands use 'cli/commands', which the docs tree adopts: each is the leaf `cli/commands/<name>`, spaces as hyphens (`theme build` is `cli/commands/theme-build`). Every command doc the CLI ships declares one, and `astryx doctor` fails on one that is missing or that nothing reads.

fields.name: aliases
fields.description: Reserved: other names for this doc. Nothing reads it today, so they do not resolve to it.

fields.name: fn
fields.description: Name of the FunctionDoc (and `@astryxdesign/cli/api` export) this command wraps.

fields.name: args
fields.description: Positional arguments.

fields.name: args[].name
fields.description: Argument name.

fields.name: args[].param
fields.description: FunctionDoc param this arg binds to; `astryx docs` shows that param's description when the arg has none.

fields.name: args[].description
fields.description: Override description. `--help` shows an argument's description only when it sets this.

fields.name: args[].required
fields.description: Whether the positional argument must be supplied.

fields.name: args[].variadic
fields.description: Whether the argument collects a variable number of values.

fields.name: options
fields.description: Flags/options.

fields.name: options[].flag
fields.description: Commander flag spec, e.g. '-l, --limit <n>' | '--json'.

fields.name: options[].param
fields.description: FunctionDoc param this flag maps to (inherits its description).

fields.name: options[].description
fields.description: Override/explicit description. Nothing requires it: a flag with neither this nor `param` shows no description.

fields.name: options[].choices
fields.description: Allowed values for the flag.

fields.name: options[].default
fields.description: Default value: a string, a boolean, or a list of strings.

fields.name: options[].cliOnly
fields.description: True for CLI-only flags with no function param (e.g. --verbose). Nothing reads it.

fields.name: subcommands
fields.description: Subcommand names (for command groups like `theme` / `layout`).

fields.name: examples
fields.description: Terminal examples.

fields.name: examples[].label
fields.description: Optional heading shown above the invocation.

fields.name: examples[].cli
fields.description: A full terminal invocation, e.g. 'astryx search button --json'.

fields.name: examples[].output
fields.description: Optional sample output.

fields.name: exitCodes
fields.description: Documented exit codes.

fields.name: exitCodes[].code
fields.description: The process exit code.

fields.name: exitCodes[].when
fields.description: The condition that produces this exit code.

fields.name: outsideProject
fields.description: What the command does outside a project. `same`: the answer it gives in a new project. `refuse`: it writes nothing and fails, naming the app project or integration package it needs. `own`: something else. Every `refuse` and `own` command also carries an `In global mode:` note in its `notes` that tells readers exactly what it does. Every command and subcommand declares one, and `astryx manifest` publishes it; a command that only groups subcommands declares none. The CLI tests run every command in an empty folder and check what it does against this value; `astryx doctor` does not check it.

fields.name: deprecated
fields.description: Deprecation notice — a DEP-* id and the replacement.

fields.name: related
fields.description: Related command names.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Freeform prose/notes.

examples.label: A command that wraps the search() function

notes.text: A command carries only CLI-surface facts. Behavior, parameters, returns, and thrown errors live in the FunctionDoc it points at via `fn`; the function does not know it has a CLI.

Bind an arg/option to a function param via `param` so it inherits that param's description: an option's in `--help` and `astryx docs`, an arg's in `astryx docs` only. Mark a flag with no function param (e.g. `--verbose`) `cliOnly: true` and give it its own `description`; nothing checks either. `--json` is a global flag, so a command doc does not declare it.

doc.name: component-doc
doc.description: The doc-type for a component directory's {Name}.doc.mjs. A discriminated union of SingleComponentDoc (props on the doc), MultiComponentDoc (a `components` array), and SubComponentDoc (a `subComponentOf` pointer). All three share the ComponentBaseDoc fields below; the variant is chosen by which of props / components / subComponentOf you set.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant for the stamped default-export format. Optional: legacy `export const docs = {...}` docs omit it and the parser falls back to shape-sniffing.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Stable machine identity without the Astryx prefix, PascalCase. e.g. 'Button', 'TextInput', 'AppShell'. For an integration component it is the export apps import: the doc sits beside the file that exports it, and when that file exports nothing under its own name, `name` may name the export it does have. Change `displayName`, not `name`, to edit the visible label; registry URLs derive from this identity by default.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Human-readable display name with spaces between words ('AppShell' → 'App Shell'). Drives the docsite gallery and sidebar label.

fields.name: registry
fields.description: Optional public registry identity. The converter derives a stable kebab-case slug from `name`; set `slug` only to override it, and keep prior relative paths in `aliases` after a published rename.

fields.name: import
fields.description: Exact public package specifier consumers use to import an integration-owned component. The packed-package gate resolves this specifier and verifies it exports the component name.

fields.name: replaces
fields.description: Integration components only: the exact `name` of the Core ComponentDoc this component takes over for unqualified lookup, so every app that loads the integration gets it from component detail, component lists, search, `swizzle <Name>`, and issue routing; `swizzle --list` keeps listing Core names. The Core original stays reachable with `--package @astryxdesign/core`. It takes effect only when the package's peer range starts at the release that applies it, `"@astryxdesign/cli": ">=0.6.7"` or later; with a lower range nothing changes and `doctor integration components` warns ({@link generic:replace-a-core-component}). Set it only to intentionally own a Core identity; give an alternative or variant its own name instead.

fields.name: deprecated
fields.description: Marks a deprecated component: it keeps working and stays documented, labeled with what replaces it. `replacement` is the `name` of the documented component to use instead; `description` is the modernization route in a sentence or two. The docsite shows a Deprecated badge in the component's page header and index tile, labels its search result, and adds a notice that links the replacement; `astryx search` results and `astryx build` kit entries carry the field. Omit it for a component that is not deprecated.

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Search keywords for CLI discovery: synonyms and related UI concepts from other design systems (MUI, Chakra, Radix, and others). Lowercase. `astryx search` matches them; `astryx component <term>` also suggests Core components by keyword.

fields.name: hiddenComponents
fields.description: Sub-component names to hide from human-facing UI (CLI listings, docs catalogs). They stay public and importable; agents and tooling can still discover them via source. In an integration it hides only full entries in this doc's `components`, which the CLI then neither lists nor opens; hide a sub-component that has its own doc with `hidden` in that doc.

fields.name: hidden
fields.description: Hide this entire component from human-facing UI. It stays public and importable. Use for a shared primitive that only makes sense inside its parent.

fields.name: group
fields.description: Optional sidebar/docs group. Clusters related components; ungrouped components appear flat in alphabetical order.

fields.name: category
fields.description: Overview-gallery category representing the component's functional role. Independent of `group` (which is for the sidebar). `Data Input` is a deprecated compatibility alias for `Form Controls`.

fields.name: isHiddenFromOverview
fields.description: Exclude from the categorized overview page while keeping the component in the sidebar and CLI. Use for sub-components or internal primitives.

fields.name: theming
fields.type: { container?: boolean; targets: ComponentThemingTarget[]; vars?: ComponentThemingVar[]; derived?: ComponentThemingDerivedVar[]; componentIcons?: ComponentIconSlotDoc[] }
fields.description: Theming configuration: the stable selector surface (astryx-* classes + data-attribute reflections) that themes target via @scope selectors in defineTheme.

fields.name: theming.container
fields.description: Marks a container component. Nothing reads it today: the theme pipeline maps `padding` to container tokens from a `theming.derived` entry `{property: 'padding', expand: 'container'}`.

fields.name: theming.targets
fields.description: Selector targets rendered by this component. Each entry corresponds to a themeProps() call in the source.

fields.name: theming.vars
fields.description: CSS custom properties exposed for theming.

fields.name: theming.derived
fields.description: Maps standard CSS properties to internal vars for theme-pipeline expansion. Ordered by priority: earlier entries emit first. The pipeline reads only Core components' entries, so an integration's have no effect.

fields.name: theming.componentIcons
fields.description: The component's icon slots, which a theme maps through `defineTheme({componentIcons})`: each slot's name, role, fallback per state, the state a slot function receives, and what `null` does. Each entry corresponds to a slot in `ComponentIconSlotMap`.

fields.name: usage
fields.description: Component usage documentation: concise summary, best practices, component-specific accessibility requirements, and optional visual anatomy. Required on a component doc; optional on a sub-component doc (`subComponentOf`), which uses its description instead.

fields.name: usage.description
fields.description: What the component is and when to use it, in 2-3 short sentences.

fields.name: usage.bestPractices
fields.description: 3-4 do/don't design-guidance items ({guidance: boolean, description: string}). Never start the description with 'Do' or 'Don't'.

fields.name: usage.accessibility
fields.description: Component-specific requirements rendered in the shared Accessibility tab. Write at about a grade-7 reading level with short sentences, common words, and active voice. For color contrast, put the ratio in `requirement`; name the exact foreground, background, state, and any overlay in `description`; explain exceptions in plain language; and give a human or agent enough detail to reproduce the check. Keep repository audit procedures in the wiki rubric.

fields.name: usage.accessibilityThemeCoverage
fields.description: Verified per-theme accessibility measurements rendered in the shared Accessibility tab. Record light and dark mode separately, include rendered color pairs, and mark failed measurements. Put visuals excluded from the audit in `notMeasured` with a short reason; do not add them as table measurements. Each theme declares `applicability` for measured values, informed by the component contract and never inferred from the ratio: `Conditional` is required only in some contexts, `Supplemental` adds another meaningful cue, and `Decorative` has no required meaning. These values do not change row status. Provide a complete breakdown when one cell summarizes multiple combinations, and protect derived values with an automated audit.

fields.name: usage.anatomy
fields.description: Structural/visual parts in reading order ({name, required, description}).

fields.name: examples
fields.description: Short code examples ({label?, code}) rendered by the CLI after the props table.

fields.name: playground
fields.description: Interactive-preview config: initial prop `defaults`, `overlay` for modal-only components, `appShellMobile` for components gated on AppShell mobile context, and a `wrapper` for context-dependent sub-components.

fields.name: props
fields.description: SingleComponentDoc variant (required there): all public props for the one primary component. Each prop is {name, type, description, default?, required?, slotElements?, stability?}. Skip styling props like xstyle/className/style. Also present on SubComponentDoc.

fields.name: components
fields.description: MultiComponentDoc variant (required there): one entry per public component/hook exported from the directory. Each entry is a full ComponentEntry (inline: name, displayName, description, props | params+returns) or a name-only ComponentRef pointing at a sibling {Name}.doc.mjs. In an integration, each full entry the module named by `import` exports is a component under its own name.

fields.name: subComponentOf
fields.description: SubComponentDoc variant (required there): the parent component's `name` (e.g. 'Chat'). Marks this file as a sub-component doc. The CLI does not copy family fields (group, category, keywords, theming, playground) from the parent to an integration's sub-component: its detail, list group and search use only what its own doc sets. Set any the child needs in its own doc.

fields.name: description
fields.description: SubComponentDoc variant (required there): one-sentence description of the sub-component's role within the parent composition. Single/Multi docs have no top-level description; they derive their summary from `usage`.

examples.label: SingleComponentDoc (props on the doc)
MultiComponentDoc (a components array)

notes.text: When it loads, a stamped component doc is checked about as loosely as an unstamped one, so adding `type: 'component'` to a doc that follows the type never breaks it: `displayName` may be missing, `category` may be any string, `usage`, `theming` and `playground` are not checked, and `examples` need only be an array. Unlike an unstamped doc, each entry in a group doc's `components` must have a `name`, and `import` and `replaces`, when set, must be non-empty strings. Write to the type anyway; it is the contract.
ComponentDoc is a discriminated union of three shapes that all extend ComponentBaseDoc. Pick the variant by which key you set: `props` (single), `components` (multi), or `subComponentOf` (sub).

items: SingleComponentDoc: one primary component; put props directly on the doc via `props`. Use for Switch, Badge, Spinner, TextInput.
MultiComponentDoc: a directory exporting several components/hooks; list them in `components` (inline ComponentEntry or name-only ComponentRef). Use for Table, Dialog, TabList.

SubComponentDoc: a single sub-component in its own {Name}.doc.mjs inside the parent directory; set `subComponentOf` to the parent name. It does not take the parent's family fields, and it may omit `usage`.

notes.label: SubComponentDoc

notes.text: The stamped format is `export default { type: 'component', ... }`, which `astryx integration add component` writes; legacy docs use `export const docs = {...}` and omit `type` (the parser shape-sniffs). A hook that is part of a component API is listed in a MultiComponentDoc `components` array: inline as a ComponentEntry (with `params`/`returns`), or by name with its own SubComponentDoc file, as Core's useTableSelection is.

doc.name: enum-doc
doc.description: The doc-type for a closed vocabulary: a fixed set of literal values such as error codes or response-type discriminants. Colocated as a `.doc.mjs` next to the source of truth it documents. Only the CLI reads enum docs, from its own source: one in an integration's docs directory fails to load, and so do that package's other docs.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant. Optional in the type, but the CLI reads a doc as an enum doc only when it is set; without it the doc drops out of the docs tree.

fields.name: name
fields.description: URL-safe identifier, used as the docs slug within its namespace.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Human-readable title.

fields.name: description
fields.description: One-line summary shown in listings.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: Optional in the type, but every doc the CLI ships declares it. The group that reads this doc. The CLI's enums use 'cli/api', which the docs tree adopts by kind: each is the leaf `cli/api/enums/<name>`. Every enum doc the CLI ships declares one, and `astryx doctor` fails on one that is missing or that nothing reads.

fields.name: aliases
fields.description: Reserved: alternate slugs for this doc. Nothing reads it today, so `astryx docs <alias>` does not open it.

fields.name: members
fields.description: The enumerated members: one entry per literal value.

fields.name: members[].value
fields.description: The literal value, e.g. 'ERR_UNKNOWN_TOPIC' | 'component.list'.

fields.name: members[].description
fields.description: What the value means / when it occurs.

fields.name: members[].deprecated
fields.description: Deprecation reason, if deprecated.

examples.label: Error-codes enum doc

notes.text: An enum doc is the human-readable mirror of a closed vocabulary defined elsewhere in source (e.g. an ERROR_CODES map or a response-type union). Keep the members in sync with that source of truth.
Mark a value with `deprecated` (a migration hint) rather than deleting it, so old codes stay documented while readers are pointed at the replacement.

doc.name: function-doc
doc.description: The generalized `type: 'function'` doc-type covering both React hooks and CLI/API functions. A hook (HookDoc) is the hook-flavored view of this same kind; FunctionDoc adds the fields an API function needs (a {type, data} return envelope, thrown error codes, the wrapping CLI command). The CLI binding itself lives in a separate CommandDoc.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant (shared with hooks).

fields.name: name
fields.description: Export name, e.g. 'search' | 'useMediaQuery'.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Human-readable display name, e.g. 'search()'.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Which flavor. Nothing reads it today: no reader sections docs by it or infers it from `importPath`. The CLI's API function docs set 'api'.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-line summary.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Longer description.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: Optional in the type, but every doc the CLI ships declares it. The group that reads this doc. The CLI's API functions use 'cli/api', which the docs tree adopts by kind: each is the leaf `cli/api/functions/<name>`, the name in kebab case (`themeUse` is `theme-use`). Every function doc the CLI ships declares one, and `astryx doctor` fails on one that is missing or that nothing reads.

fields.name: aliases
fields.description: Reserved: other names for this doc. Nothing reads it today, so they do not resolve to it.

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Search keywords for discovery.

fields.name: importPath
fields.description: Import path, e.g. '@astryxdesign/cli/api' | '@astryxdesign/core/hooks'.

fields.name: signature
fields.description: Full signature as a string, e.g. 'search(query, options?): Promise<SearchResponse>'.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Parameters / options-object fields.

fields.name: params[].name
fields.description: Parameter or option field name.

fields.name: params[].type
fields.description: TypeScript type signature as a string.

fields.name: params[].description
fields.description: What this parameter does. 1-2 sentences.

fields.name: params[].default
fields.description: Default value as a string, if optional with a default.

fields.name: params[].required
fields.description: True if required. Omit if optional.

fields.name: returns
fields.description: Return documentation. Hooks list named return fields (`name` set); API functions list {type, data} envelope entries where `type` is the response discriminant and `name` is omitted.

fields.name: returns[].name
fields.description: Field name (hooks); omit for API envelope entries.

fields.name: returns[].type
fields.description: TS type (hooks) or response-type discriminant (API), as a string.

fields.name: returns[].description
fields.description: What this return value / envelope entry provides.

fields.name: throws
fields.description: Errors the function throws (API functions), keyed to ERROR_CODES.

fields.name: throws[].code
fields.description: The ERROR_CODES member thrown.

fields.name: throws[].when
fields.description: The condition under which it is thrown.

fields.name: examples
fields.description: Usage examples.

fields.name: examples[].label
fields.description: Optional heading shown above the snippet.

fields.name: examples[].code
fields.description: Language-level usage, e.g. "await search('button')".

fields.name: examples[].result
fields.description: Optional sample result.

fields.name: usage
fields.description: Usage documentation (hooks): description, best practices, accessibility requirements, and anatomy. Same shape as HookDoc.usage.

fields.name: command
fields.description: The CLI command that wraps this function, e.g. 'search'.

fields.name: related
fields.description: Related function names; the CLI links each to its doc. Name the CLI command with `command`, not here.

fields.name: relatedComponents
fields.description: Component names this is commonly used with (hooks).

fields.name: relatedHooks
fields.description: Other hook names this is commonly used with (hooks).

fields.name: category
fields.description: Category for grouping in listings.

examples.label: An API function doc (envelope return, no field name)

notes.text: `parseDoc` accepts a stamped function doc without `displayName` and does not check its `usage`, and the CLI reads its own function docs without checking them. Write to the type anyway; it is the contract.
The `type` discriminant is 'function' for both flavors. `kind: 'hook'` or `kind: 'api'` names the flavor; nothing reads it today.

The two flavors differ in `returns`: a hook lists named fields (`name` set), while an API function lists {type, data} envelope entries whose `type` is the response discriminant and whose `name` is omitted. `throws` (keyed to ERROR_CODES) applies to API functions.

The function does not know it has a CLI. The terminal binding (args, flags, exit codes) lives in a separate CommandDoc that references this function via `fn`; here you only note the wrapping command name via `command`.

doc.name: hook-doc
doc.description: The doc-type for a standalone React hook (e.g. useMediaQuery, useFocusTrap, useOverflow) that gets its own `.doc.mjs`. Hooks that are part of a component API (e.g. useImperativeDialog) belong in that component's MultiComponentDoc `components` array instead. `HookDoc` is the hook-flavored view of the shared `type: 'function'` kind. `astryx hook` reads Core's hook docs only; an integration lists its hooks in a component doc's `components` array.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant (shared with FunctionDoc). Legacy `export const docs = {...}` docs omit it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Stable hook name exactly as exported, e.g. 'useMediaQuery', 'useFocusTrap'. Change `displayName`, not `name`, to edit the visible label; registry URLs derive from this identity by default.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Human-readable display name. Hooks read better as the raw identifier ('useMediaQuery') than spaced, so keep the identifier verbatim.

fields.name: registry
fields.description: Optional public registry identity. The converter derives a stable kebab-case slug from `name`; set `slug` only to override it, and keep prior relative paths in `aliases` after a published rename.

fields.name: group
fields.description: Optional group for sidebar/docs organization; same as ComponentDoc.group.

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Search keywords for CLI discovery.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Hook parameters or options-object fields.

fields.name: params[].name
fields.description: Parameter or option field name.

fields.name: params[].type
fields.description: TypeScript type signature as a string.

fields.name: params[].description
fields.description: What this parameter does. 1-2 sentences.

fields.name: params[].default
fields.description: Default value as a string, if optional with a default.

fields.name: params[].required
fields.description: True if required. Omit if optional.

fields.name: returns
fields.description: Return value documentation. For object returns, list each field; for primitive returns, use a single entry.

fields.name: returns[].name
fields.description: Field name on the returned object, or 'value' for primitive returns.

fields.name: returns[].type
fields.description: TypeScript type.

fields.name: returns[].description
fields.description: What this return value provides.

fields.name: usage
fields.description: Usage documentation: description and best practices.

fields.name: usage.description
fields.description: What the hook is and when to use it, in 2-3 short sentences.

fields.name: usage.bestPractices
fields.description: 3-4 do/don't design-guidance items ({guidance: boolean, description: string}).

fields.name: usage.accessibility
fields.description: Accessibility requirements specific to using the hook ({name, description}).

fields.name: usage.anatomy
fields.description: Structural/visual anatomy elements (rarely used for hooks).

fields.name: relatedComponents
fields.description: Component names this hook is commonly used with. Enables cross-referencing (e.g. `astryx hook useToast` links back to Toast).

fields.name: relatedHooks
fields.description: Other hook names this hook is commonly used with.

fields.name: importPath
fields.description: Import path, e.g. '@astryxdesign/core/hooks' or '@astryxdesign/core/Toast'.

fields.name: category
fields.description: Category for grouping in listings.

examples.label: A standalone hook doc

notes.text: `parseDoc` accepts a stamped hook doc without `displayName` and does not check its `usage`, and `astryx hook` prints a hook doc without checking it at all. Write to the type anyway; it is the contract.
A hook's discriminant is `type: 'function'`: HookDoc and FunctionDoc share the generalized function kind. HookDoc is the hook-flavored view: named `returns` fields and a required `usage` block.

A hook that is part of a component API is listed in that component's MultiComponentDoc `components` array: inline with `params`/`returns`, or by name with its own SubComponentDoc file, as Core's useTableSelection is.

doc.name: icon-definition-doc
doc.description: Experimental: may change or be removed in a patch release. One thing an icon can stand for, such as `close` or `delete`. Astryx ships one file per definition; an icon set adds its own in the same format. A set's data file `map` registers which of its icons draws each definition.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant.

fields.name: name
fields.description: camelCase identity: the key a data file's `map` uses. Must match the file name.

fields.name: description
fields.description: One sentence: what an icon with this definition is for.

fields.name: words
fields.description: Lower-case terms a person might search for; at least one.

fields.name: builtIn
fields.description: Only on Astryx's own definitions: the definition is a shared icon name Core renders, so every icon set maps it.

fields.name: stability
fields.description: Marks the definition as experimental: the icon-definitions listing shows it as `[experimental]`. Omit it for a definition you mean to keep.

examples.label: A set's own definition at icon-sets/outline/definitions/random.doc.mjs

notes.text: A set's own definitions sit in a `definitions` folder in the set's directory, one file per definition. Its `map` registers icons for them like for Astryx's. `astryx docs cli/experimental/icon-definitions` lists every definition: Astryx's, and, in a project that sets `experimental.iconSet`, those of each installed set. A definition file refuses a field it does not know.

IconDefinitionDoc is static metadata: one default-exported object of literal fields directly under a `/** @type {import('@astryxdesign/cli/authoring').IconDefinitionDoc} */` comment. Discovery reads it without executing it.
To share a definition with every set, copy its file into Astryx's definitions folder in a pull request.

doc.name: icon-set-data
doc.description: Experimental: may change or be removed in a patch release. An icon set's data file: which icons exist, the export that draws each one, the words a person might search for, and which icon draws each icon definition (`map`). `astryx experimental icon`, template icon mapping, and the checks read this file and nothing else.

fields.name: schemaVersion
fields.description: Data-file format version.

fields.name: module
fields.description: The import specifier every `export` is read from: the set's own package name, or one of its package.json `exports` subpaths. Never a file path.

fields.name: source
fields.description: The upstream library and version the file was generated from. Omit it for a set with no upstream.

fields.name: exclude
fields.description: Library exports that are not icons. `experimental icon new-set --from` leaves them out every time it wraps or refreshes the set; `--exclude` adds to the list. A CLI whose reference does not list this key withdraws a set that sets it, naming the key; leave it out for a set those CLIs must read.

fields.name: generated
fields.description: The module `astryx experimental icon add` writes, as a `./` path from the package root: one export per icon, a re-export of a library component or the adapter applied to a library export, and `themeIcons`, the theme map, from the built-in entries of `map`. The CLI writes its declaration file beside it. The package's entry re-exports it.

fields.name: adapter
fields.description: A function in the package, `(source) => Component`, that turns a library export that is not a component (icon data, an SVG string or URL) into one. `module` is a `./` path from the package root.

fields.name: variants
fields.description: The named looks the set offers, in lower-kebab case, such as `outline` and `solid`. Icon size is never a variant: CSS sets it. Omit it when the set has one look.

fields.name: default
fields.description: The variant each icon's own `export` draws; one of `variants`.

fields.name: themeMap
fields.description: The export that maps each built-in icon definition to its artwork, keyed by exactly the built-in definitions in `map`.

fields.name: map
fields.description: Which of this set's icons draws each icon definition: definition name to icon `id`. Keys are Astryx's definitions (`astryx docs cli/experimental/icon-definitions`) or ones the set declares in its `definitions` folder, one file per definition. One icon may draw several definitions; each definition maps to one icon. Every built-in definition must be mapped.

fields.name: icons
fields.description: Every icon in the set.

fields.name: icons[].id
fields.description: Lower-kebab identity, unique in the set.

fields.name: icons[].export
fields.description: The named export that draws the icon's default variant, named `<Name>Icon`: a React component that takes SVG props and draws with `currentColor`.

fields.name: icons[].module
fields.description: The import specifier, when it differs from the set's `module`.

fields.name: icons[].words
fields.description: Lower-case terms a person might search for, the words of the icon's own name included; at least one. Do not copy the words of the definitions `map` names the icon for: search already matches the icon by them.

fields.name: icons[].variants
fields.description: Other variants of the icon: each names one of `variants`, never the default, and the export that draws it. At most one export per variant.

fields.name: icons[].matches
fields.description: Reviewed equivalents of this icon in other icon sets or libraries, such as `{set: 'lines', export: 'CrossIcon', variant: 'solid', confidence: 'exact'}`. When a copied template imports a matched icon from that installed set, `exact` and `strong` matches are used before any other rule; a `likely` match is only suggested. A match never names this set itself.

notes.text: A file that fails this schema, repeats an id, gives an icon no words, has a `map` key that is not camelCase or a `map` value that is not an icon id in the file, or names a variant `variants` does not declare is invalid, and its set is withdrawn from every surface until it is fixed. `astryx doctor` names the reason.

A template declares the icon definition each icon it imports draws. With a project icon set, each declared icon maps to the icon whose `matches` name it with `exact` or `strong` confidence (for an icon another installed set ships), else to the icon this file's `map` names for its definition. Nothing is guessed from names or words.

Write it with the CLI: `astryx experimental icon add` registers one icon and its `map` entry, `astryx experimental icon map` changes an entry, and `astryx experimental icon new-set --from` wraps a whole library.

doc.name: icon-set-doc
doc.description: Experimental: may change or be removed in a patch release. The strongly typed descriptor for one icon set an integration ships: what a person writes about the set. The set's icons, and what each one means, live in the `<name>.icons.json` data file beside it.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Lower-kebab icon-set identity. Must match the descriptor parent directory.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Human-readable name shown by `astryx experimental icon --list`.

fields.name: description
fields.description: One-line summary shown by `astryx experimental icon --list`.

fields.name: maintained
fields.description: Whether the owning package actively maintains this set.

fields.name: license
fields.description: SPDX license expression for the artwork.

examples.label: An icon-set descriptor at icons/outline/outline.doc.mjs

notes.text: Point the manifest's `experimental.iconSets` field at the folder that holds your sets. Each lower-kebab folder under it is one set, named by the folder, and holds `<name>.doc.mjs`, `<name>.icons.json`, and any license notice files. The manifest never lists sets or icons.

Write the descriptor as one default-exported object of literal strings and booleans under a `/** @type {import('@astryxdesign/cli/authoring').IconSetDoc} */` comment, with nothing else in the file. Discovery reads it, and the data file, without executing them or the icon module.

The data file is described by {@link schema:icon-set-data}. Run `astryx integration check` to prove every export it names exists in the module and that the theme map agrees with the built-in entries of `map`.

doc.name: namespace-doc
doc.description: Declares one level of the docs tree: named slots, and adoption rules for already-discovered docs. It never scans folders, lists its children, or copies child documents: a child names its parent with `placement`, or a namespace adopts a discovery group. `astryx docs <route>` lists each slot's children one level down. The CLI keeps its namespace docs in its docs tree directory; an integration ships its own in its docs directory, and they appear in `astryx docs` beside the CLI's.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Stable provider-local identity. Moving the namespace does not change this value.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Human-readable page title.

fields.name: summary
fields.description: One-line summary used in listings and search results.

fields.name: placement
fields.description: Optional canonical parent: {parent, slot?, order?}. `parent` names a namespace of the same package as `namespace:<name>`. An invalid placement withdraws the namespace with a diagnostic; it never falls back.

fields.name: aliases
fields.description: Prior names or routes the docs tree will keep resolving to this doc. Not read yet.

fields.name: audience
fields.description: Reserved: bundle audience. Nothing reads it yet: a namespace that sets 'internal' still shows in `astryx docs`.

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Search terms not already present in the title or summary.

fields.name: slots
fields.description: Named placement and collection targets. Each slot declares a title and the doc kinds it accepts. `accepts.providers` is not read yet: only docs of the namespace's own package can be placed in a slot.

fields.name: adopts
fields.description: Provider-local rules that adopt otherwise-unplaced docs from a logical discovery group. They never scan a folder.

fields.name: adopts[].source.packages
fields.description: Experimental: may change or be removed in a patch release. `'all'` adopts the group from every package, not only the namespace's own, and is read only on the CLI's own namespaces that are marked `stability: 'experimental'`.

fields.name: blocks
fields.description: Ordered layout content for the namespace page. Graph-only workflow, collection, and reference blocks are available here without widening the stable ReferenceContentBlock union used by existing topic renderers. `astryx docs <route>` prints the prose, heading, code, table, and list blocks above the slots, and `--json` returns every block with its links resolved. A collection block is not rendered yet, and `astryx doctor` warns on one.

examples.label: A CLI namespace with one adopted source group

notes.text: The docs tree reads namespace docs from the CLI and from every configured integration. An integration's namespace doc without a `placement` is a top-level level of the tree, and its guides name it with `placement`; a doc can be placed only in a namespace of its own package. When two packages claim one route, the CLI's own docs win, then integrations in configured order, and `astryx doctor` names the loser.

Child docs request one canonical home with placement. A collection block refers to those docs by stable reference and never creates a second identity or parent. It is not rendered yet: `astryx doctor` warns on one.

items: Use a directory as implicit navigation.
Put JSX, HTML, ANSI, callbacks, or custom renderer code in a doc.
Use choice, callout, or checklist blocks before the full block-extension contract exists.

doc.name: reference-doc
doc.description: The doc-type for a reference/topic doc: tokens, principles, theming, patterns, accessibility, migration guides. Unlike ComponentDoc it is not tied to a component: drop a `.doc.mjs` in the docs directory and it shows up in `astryx docs`. Content is built from ordered sections of mixed content blocks.
doc.appliesTo: <topic>.doc.{ts,mjs,js} in the folder the integration manifest's `docs` names

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant. Stays 'generic' (the reference/topic discriminant). Legacy `export const docs = {...}` docs omit it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: URL-safe identifier, used as the CLI topic name. e.g. 'tokens', 'principles'.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Human-readable title. e.g. 'All Tokens'. (Reference docs use `title`, not `displayName`.)

fields.name: description
fields.description: One-line summary shown in topic listings.

fields.name: category
fields.description: Navigation category: 'guide' or 'foundations'.

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Words a reader may search for that the title and sections do not use: a synonym, a task, or another library's name for the same thing. `astryx search` matches each as a keyword of the whole topic, so an exact one ranks the topic like its own title does.

fields.name: replaces
fields.description: Name of an existing topic this doc takes the place of. Authored by an integration that serves its own guide instead of the built-in one: on a doc of the same name it swaps the content, and on a doc of another name it also leaves the old name as an alias so `astryx docs <old>` still resolves. Exclusive with `extends`.

fields.name: extends
fields.description: Name of an existing topic this doc merges onto, section by section. A section replaces the base section with the same `id`, or else the one with exactly its title when either of the two has no `id`. A key derived from a title counts only against an `id`: a section without an `id` also matches a base section whose `id` is the key its title derives, and a section with an `id` also matches a base section without one whose title derives that `id`. Two different `id`s never match, two sections without an `id` whose titles differ only in case or punctuation stay separate, and a section that matches none is appended. The topic keeps the base's title and description. For correcting or adding to a topic rather than owning it. Exclusive with `replaces`.

fields.name: sections
fields.description: Ordered sections that make up the doc. Each becomes an h2 in full output and can be retrieved via `astryx docs <topic> <section>`.

fields.name: sections[].id
fields.description: Stable section anchor. New docs should set this instead of relying on a mutable title. Published @astryxdesign/cli 0.6.3 and earlier reject the field and hide every doc topic the package ships, so `astryx integration verify` fails an integration that sets one until it declares an `@astryxdesign/cli` peer of `>=0.6.4`.

fields.name: sections[].title
fields.description: Section title, e.g. "Spacing Tokens", "Light/Dark Mode".

fields.name: sections[].category
fields.description: Navigation category ('guide' | 'foundations'). Mirrors the parent doc's category so sections can be grouped independently.

fields.name: sections[].content
fields.description: Ordered content blocks: prose, heading, code, table, list, token-ref, and reference. A `reference` block (`{type: 'reference', target, projection?, presentation?}`) includes another doc from its canonical source instead of a copy: a schema, command, function, or enum doc as `astryx docs` prints it, then the command that opens it. `projection.fields` keeps only those fields of a schema; `presentation` is `full` (the default), `compact` (no code blocks), or `summary` (only the doc's title, summary, and command). Any other doc shows as a summary. Graph-only workflow and collection blocks are available through GraphContentBlock on NamespaceDoc, without widening the stable ReferenceContentBlock union. Inside text, `{@link <target>}` links another doc by identity (`[<provider>:]<kind>:<name>`): the CLI prints the command that opens it, and `astryx doctor` warns on one that names no doc.

fields.name: sections[].previewType
