fields.description: Preview type for token tables in this section. The CLI rejects a value not in the list below and returns the value in `astryx docs --json`, but draws no preview from it. Omit for non-token sections.

fields.name: tokenCategory
fields.description: Token category for foundational docs that map to a token section (e.g. 'color'). `astryx docs --json` returns it as authored; no tokens page links to the doc through it.

examples.label: A reference doc with one section

notes.text: A stamped generic doc without `title`, `description` or `sections` still loads, as older codemod output does; its title falls back to `displayName` or `name`. Without a description and sections it is not a usable topic, and `astryx doctor` reports it.

Each `sections[].content` is an ordered array of ReferenceContentBlock, the stable discriminated union of prose, heading, code, table, list, and token-ref, plus the reference block (ReferenceDocBlock). A read inlines a reference block the way it inlines a token-ref, so `astryx docs`, in text and in `--json`, returns only the stable block kinds. Docs-graph-only workflow and collection blocks are exported separately as GraphContentBlock and accepted by NamespaceDoc. choice, callout, and checklist remain invalid. ReferenceContentBlock is also reused by the `notes` field on SchemaDoc and CommandDoc. Inside text, `{@link <target>}` links another doc by identity (`[<provider>:]<kind>:<name>`): the CLI prints the command that opens it, and `astryx doctor` warns on one that names no doc. Write a CLI command in text, shell code, or a table cell as a bare `astryx` command: a text read adds the runner the reader uses in front of it, and `--json` returns it as written.

A reference block includes content, where a link only points at it: `astryx doctor integration docs` fails when its target names no doc, when `projection.fields` names a field the schema does not have, or when the doc cannot take the projection or presentation it sets, and a read marks the missing content. A target without a provider names a doc of the package that wrote it, so an integration names the CLI's docs with the CLI's provider, as in `@astryxdesign/cli:schema:integration`.

notes.label: A section that includes two fields of the integration manifest
ReferenceContentBlock union

notes.text: A `token-ref` block (e.g. {type: 'token-ref', topic: 'tokens', section: 'Color Tokens'}) references a token table in another topic; the CLI resolves and inlines it at read time so the docsite can render live theme values.

A section may set `previewType`, a hint for previewing its token table, to one of 'swatch' | 'shadow-box' | 'radius-box' | 'spacing-bar' | 'size-bar' | 'border-line' | 'duration-bar' | 'easing-curve' | 'font-sample'; the CLI rejects any other value.

doc.name: schema-doc
doc.description: The doc-type for documenting an authored/received OBJECT shape (astryx.config, a codemod payload, the doc-types themselves). Colocated as a `.doc.mjs` next to the schema it describes. Fields nest recursively, so a whole shape is one tree.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant. Marks the file as a schema doc.

fields.name: name
fields.description: URL-safe identifier, used as the docs slug within its namespace.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Human-readable title.

fields.name: description
fields.description: One-line summary shown in listings.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: The group that reads this doc: 'authoring' for a file an author writes (a section of {@link generic:field-reference}), or 'cli/api' for a shape the CLI returns (the docs tree adopts it by kind, as the leaf `cli/api/schemas/<name>`). Every schema doc the CLI ships declares one, and `astryx doctor` fails on one that is missing or that nothing reads.

fields.name: aliases
fields.description: Reserved: alternate slugs for this doc. Nothing reads it yet: `astryx docs` finds a schema doc by its `name` only.

fields.name: appliesTo
fields.description: What this schema applies to, e.g. 'astryx.config.{ts,mjs,js}' | 'AstryxConfig'.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: The fields that make up the shape. Object-typed fields nest their members recursively via each field's own `fields`, so the whole shape is one tree.

fields.name: fields[].name
fields.description: Field name, or a dotted path for a nested field (e.g. 'hooks.postCodemod').

fields.name: fields[].type
fields.description: TypeScript type signature as a string, e.g. 'string[]' | "'a' | 'b'".

fields.name: fields[].description
fields.description: What the field is for, in 1-2 sentences.

fields.name: fields[].required
fields.description: True if the field must be provided. Omit (don't set false) if optional.

fields.name: fields[].default
fields.description: Default value as a string, if any.

fields.name: fields[].example
fields.description: A short inline example value.

fields.name: fields[].deprecated
fields.description: Deprecation reason, if the field is deprecated.

fields.name: fields[].fields
fields.description: Nested object fields, for object-typed fields. Recursive.

fields.name: examples
fields.description: Full example objects/snippets.

fields.name: examples[].label
fields.description: Optional heading shown above the snippet.

fields.name: examples[].code
fields.description: The example source.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Freeform prose/notes rendered after the field table and examples. The stable ReferenceContentBlock union (prose, heading, code, table, list, token-ref), without the reference block a ReferenceDoc section also takes; a token-ref note is accepted but not rendered.

examples.label: A small schema doc with a nested object field

notes.text: SchemaFieldDoc is recursive: an object-typed field lists its members in its own `fields`, so an entire nested shape (including paths like `hooks.postCodemod` or `experimental.xle.components`) is documented as one tree.
Name nested fields with a dotted path from the root (e.g. `hooks.postCodemod`) so readers can see where each field sits in the shape.

items: Set `required: true` only for mandatory fields.
Keep `type` close to the real TS type; use single quotes for string-literal unions.
Set `required: false` for optional fields; omit `required` entirely instead.

doc.name: integration-template-doc
doc.description: The doc-type for an integration package's template metadata. It has every TemplateDoc field and rule, except that `category` is the package's own string instead of a TemplateCategory value.

fields.name: category
fields.description: The package's own category. Bare `astryx template` groups the package's templates by it.

examples.label: Block template in an integration package

notes.text: Every other field, and the page and block variants, are TemplateDoc's. Core's own templates use TemplateDoc, whose `category` is a TemplateCategory value. `astryx doctor integration validate` checks an integration's template docs against IntegrationTemplateDoc.

doc.name: template-doc
doc.description: The doc-type for template metadata. A discriminated union of PageTemplateDoc (type: 'page') for full page templates and BlockTemplateDoc (type: 'block') for editable compositions. A block can stand alone or use `exampleFor` to attach to one component; `isShowcase` requires that component ownership.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Discriminant selecting the variant: 'page' for a full page template, 'block' for an editable composition that may be standalone or component-owned.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Stable identifier for block templates; change `displayName`, not `name`, to edit their visible label in the gallery. For page templates it is a human-readable label, while the existing template-directory/CLI slug owns the default registry path. `astryx template --list` and `astryx search` print `name` as the label of both, and `astryx template <id>` finds a template by its id, never by `name`: an integration template's id is its path under the templates folder without the `.doc.*` suffix.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Human-readable label for the gallery. The CLI prints `name` instead; `astryx template --list --json` also returns an integration template's `displayName`. Spaces out block names that mirror a PascalCase component ('ChatMessageMetadata' → 'Chat Message Metadata').

fields.name: registry
fields.description: Optional public registry identity. The converter derives a stable kebab-case slug from `name` (or the existing page-template slug); set `slug` only to override it, and keep prior relative paths in `aliases` after a published rename.

fields.name: description
fields.description: One-sentence description of what the template provides.

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Search keywords for CLI discovery: the ideas, domains, and other names a builder might use for what the template serves (e.g. ['monitoring', 'uptime', 'on-call'] for a service-health dashboard). Lowercase. `astryx search` matches them as it matches the description and `astryx build` ranks page templates on them, so keep them out of `description`. Integration templates need @astryxdesign/cli 0.6.6 or later: earlier CLIs reject the field and drop that template, and CLIs before 0.6.4 also hide the package's doc topics.

fields.name: replaces
fields.description: Integration templates only: the exact id of the Core template this one replaces for unqualified lookup. Find it with `astryx --json template --list --package @astryxdesign/core`; the Core original stays selectable with `--package @astryxdesign/core`. A page replaces only a Core page and a block only a Core block. Needs @astryxdesign/cli 0.6.4 or later: earlier CLIs reject the field, drop that template, and hide the package's doc topics.

fields.name: icons
fields.description: The icon definition each icon the source imports draws, such as `{TrashIcon: 'delete'}`: a named import is keyed by the name it imports (`{Trash as TrashIcon}` is `Trash`), a default import by its local name (`import DeleteIcon from …` is `DeleteIcon`). When the project sets `experimental.iconSet`, `astryx template` (shown or copied) replaces each declared icon with the set's icon for that definition (`astryx docs cli/experimental/icon-definitions`) and reports every key as mapped or kept; an undeclared import is left alone. A name imported from two modules (`TrashIcon` from an outline and a solid module) needs one key, and each import keeps its variant when its module belongs to an installed set.

fields.name: isReady
fields.description: Whether the template is ready for use. false shows as '(WIP)' in the gallery and CLI.

fields.name: scaffold
fields.description: Scaffolding-only template (e.g. blank page): available via the CLI but hidden from browsable galleries.

fields.name: category
fields.description: Functional gallery category following a 'Group - Variant' convention (e.g. 'Dashboard - Analytics', 'Table - Basic', 'Form - Wizard'). The overview groups by the text before ' - '.

fields.name: isHiddenFromOverview
fields.description: Opt out of the Templates overview gallery while staying available via the CLI. Use for duplicate/experimental variants. Scaffold templates are hidden automatically.

fields.name: exampleFor
fields.description: Block templates only: optional component ownership. Set this when the block is specifically an example of one component. Omit it for a standalone composition.

fields.name: alsoExampleFor
fields.description: Block templates only: additional component/hook doc pages whose Examples section should include this block.

fields.name: alsoShowcaseFor
fields.description: Block templates only: additional doc pages whose hero showcase should reuse this block (secondary placements; does not change the primary showcase).

fields.name: aspectRatio
fields.description: Block templates only (required): width-to-height ratio for preview containers (e.g. 16/9, 1, 3/4).

fields.name: scale
fields.description: Block templates only: scale factor for the block preview.

fields.name: componentsUsed
fields.description: Block templates only: component names this block uses, for 'See also'/'Used in' cross-references (not primary attribution).

fields.name: isShowcase
fields.description: Block templates only: when true this block is the canonical hero showcase for its `exampleFor` component. Requires `exampleFor`.

examples.label: Page template
Block template (component example)

notes.text: When it loads, a template may leave out `displayName` and `aspectRatio` and use its own `category`, as integration templates already published do; a block with no `aspectRatio` previews at 1. Write to the type anyway; it is the contract, and `astryx doctor integration validate` warns about an integration template that leaves out `displayName` or `aspectRatio`.

TemplateDoc is a discriminated union keyed by `type`. Set `type: 'page'` for a full page template. Set `type: 'block'` for an editable composition; add `exampleFor` only when one component owns the example.

items: PageTemplateDoc (type: 'page'): a full page template; `name` doubles as its display value.
BlockTemplateDoc (type: 'block'): an editable composition. `exampleFor` is optional component ownership; omit it for a standalone block. `isShowcase` requires `exampleFor`.

notes.text: `category` uses the shared TemplateCategory taxonomy: 'Group - Variant' strings (e.g. 'Table - Bulk Actions'). Not every value maps to an existing template; unused values are reserved so authors get autocomplete for the full taxonomy.

doc.name: theme-doc
doc.description: The strongly typed descriptor for one source theme: bundled with the CLI, shipped by an integration, or kept in the project's src/themes, where `theme eject` writes one.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Doc-kind discriminant.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Lower-kebab CLI theme identity. Must match the descriptor parent directory.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Human-readable name shown by theme listings.

fields.name: description
fields.description: One-line summary shown by theme listings.

fields.name: maintained
fields.description: Whether the owning package actively maintains this theme.

examples.label: A theme descriptor beside oceanTheme.ts

notes.text: ThemeDoc is static metadata. The descriptor holds one default-exported object of literal string and boolean fields, directly under a `/** @type {import('@astryxdesign/cli/authoring').ThemeDoc} */` comment, and nothing else: without that comment, or with any other statement, it fails to load. Discovery validates it without executing the descriptor or theme source.
The descriptor and source share one stem. For oceanTheme.doc.mjs, discovery requires exactly one oceanTheme source module and a named oceanTheme runtime export.
The parent theme directory, including this descriptor, is the complete copy and pack boundary. Nested source, palettes, assets, and receipts need no second file list.

doc.name: gap-report-handler
doc.description: A handler for `{@command gap-report}`: a plain object with an `audience` and a `handle` function. Set it as `gapReport` in astryx.config, or export it as `gapReport` from an integration manifest. Handlers add up rather than replace each other: the project handler first, then each loaded integration's in load order (the `integrations` list, then autolinked ones), whichever package the report is about.
doc.appliesTo: `gapReport` in astryx.config.*, or the `gapReport` named export of astryx.integration.*

fields.name: audience
fields.description: Whether the destination is internal to your organization or public. A public handler runs only when the caller agrees; an internal handler always runs.

fields.name: handle
fields.description: Gets the report and returns a receipt. It can be async, and the CLI waits at most 30 seconds for it. A throw, a timeout, or an invalid receipt is a failed delivery, and the other handlers still run.

fields.name: report
fields.description: The report. Each handler gets its own copy.

fields.name: report.schemaVersion
fields.description: Version of the report shape.

fields.name: report.component
fields.description: The component the gap is about.

fields.name: report.category
fields.description: The kind of gap: 'missing_component', 'missing_variant', 'layout_gap', 'styling_gap', 'a11y_gap', 'api_friction', 'docs_gap', or 'other'.

fields.name: report.categoryLabel
fields.description: A readable name for the category.

fields.name: report.intention
fields.description: What the caller was trying to do.

fields.name: report.detail
fields.description: More detail, when the caller gave some.

fields.name: report.source
fields.description: Who sent the report: 'human', 'ai', 'automation', or 'unknown'.

fields.name: report.timestamp
fields.description: When the report was sent, as ISO 8601.

fields.name: report.target
fields.description: The package the report is about.

fields.name: report.target.package
fields.description: The package name.

fields.name: report.target.version
fields.description: The integration's version from its package.json. Null for Core, and when the package.json has none.

fields.name: report.target.issuesUrl
fields.description: Where the package takes issues. Null when it does not say.

fields.name: context
fields.description: The context of this call.

fields.name: context.signal
fields.description: Aborted when the handler runs past 30 seconds.

examples.label: A project handler in astryx.config

rows: 'filed': the handler created or queued the report. 'routed_only': it points to a place to file the report, and must return `url`. 'skipped': it chose not to act, for example on a duplicate.
An http or https URL. Required when status is routed_only.
A readable message of at most 2000 characters.

notes.text: The receipt is strict: an unknown field, a URL that is not http or https, or a filed or routed_only receipt with neither `url` nor `message` is invalid.

doc.name: provider-identity
doc.description: Separates stable provider/artifact identity from package instances and runtime lifecycle state. Provider identity names integration manifests and settles provider conflicts. Docs-tree nodes are identified by doc identity; the tree covers the CLI's docs and each integration's. Artifact IDs for kinds outside the docs tree, provider instances, and compiler-input entries are defined for every provider-owned artifact; no command builds them.
doc.appliesTo: Integration manifests, provider conflicts, and docs-tree node ids.

fields.name: ProviderId
fields.description: Canonical logical provider ID. It defaults to the lowercase npm package name; Core uses the same model without publishing an integration manifest.

fields.name: ArtifactId
fields.description: Versioned serialization of provider ID, contribution kind, and stable artifact name. Every segment uses RFC 3986 escaping.

fields.name: DocId
fields.description: Artifact ID restricted to one authored doc kind. Navigation changes do not change it.

fields.name: ProviderInstance
fields.description: One immutable package version and source/content digest. It carries no installed, configured, loaded, selected, or healthy state.

fields.name: AuthoredDocEntry
fields.type: { id; provider; kind; stableName; source; authored }
fields.description: Normalized compiler input. `stableName`, the key in its doc ID, is given separately from the authored display name; source paths remain package-relative, and provider provenance plus the authored snapshot are immutable.

notes.text: Provider package renames require an explicit mapping: a ProviderInstance may retain its stable providerId while packageName changes. Silent identity changes are not inferred.

doc.name: integration
doc.description: The astryx.integration.* manifest that sits beside an integration package's package.json. It can preserve a stable provider identity across a package rename, and points the CLI at the package's components, templates, codemods, doc topics, source themes, managed agent guidance, issue tracker, and the command its users run the CLI with. Every field is optional.

fields.name: providerId
fields.description: The name that marks this package as the source of everything it contributes. Leave it out to use the package name from package.json. Set it to the old name only during a rename, so the IDs of what the package already contributed stay the same. If two packages use the same name here, the one you are working on wins; otherwise the one the CLI reads first wins, and the CLI warns about the other.

fields.name: components
fields.description: The folder that holds your components and their docs, relative to package.json.

fields.name: templates
fields.description: The folder that holds your templates, relative to package.json.

fields.name: codemods
fields.description: The folder that holds your codemods, relative to package.json.

fields.name: docs
fields.description: The folder that holds your doc topics, relative to package.json. Every {topic}.doc.{ts,mjs,js} under it shows up in `{@command docs}`: a flat topic next to the built-in topics, where it can set `replaces` or `extends` to take over a built-in topic or add to it, and a guide with `placement` at its own route in the docs tree, under a namespace doc of the same package.

fields.name: themes
fields.description: The folder that holds your themes, relative to package.json, with one folder per theme. Each theme folder has the theme source and a matching .doc.mjs file with the same name. Installed themes show up in `{@command theme list}`; `theme add` imports their built package exports, and `theme eject` creates an editable local fork.

fields.name: experimental
fields.description: Experimental contribution roots: they may change or be removed in a patch release.

fields.name: experimental.iconSets
fields.description: Experimental: may change or be removed in a patch release. The folder that holds your icon sets, relative to package.json, with one folder per set. Each set folder has a matching `<name>.doc.mjs` IconSetDoc and a `<name>.icons.json` data file. Installed sets answer `astryx experimental icon`; a project that sets `experimental.iconSet` gets copied templates in that set's icons.

fields.name: agentDocs
fields.description: Lines of guidance your package adds to the end of the agent instructions the CLI manages. The CLI owns the heading, labels, bullets, and which files it writes.

fields.name: issuesUrl
fields.description: Where people file issues for this package: an absolute URL, such as its GitHub issues page. A value that is not a URL fails the whole manifest; the scheme is not checked. Nothing warns when it is missing, but without it `{@command gap-report}` about this package fails unless the project or a loaded integration has a gapReport handler, and `{@command swizzle}` prints no feedback link for this package's components. When no handler is loaded, a github.com issues URL is filed with the GitHub CLI once the reporter passes `--confirm-public`; any other URL is returned for the reporter to open.

fields.name: docsiteUrl
fields.description: Link to this integration's docs site, such as its home page. Catalogs that list the package may show it.

fields.name: cliCommand
fields.description: The command your users run the Astryx CLI with, when it is not their package manager, such as a wrapper your company ships. Every command the CLI prints in an app that loads your package starts with it, in place of `pnpm exec astryx` or `yarn astryx`: hints, errors, Doctor fixes, and doc text. One line, without a subcommand. If two loaded packages set different commands, neither is used and `{@command doctor}` warns. An invalid value is ignored with an `invalid_cli_command` warning, and the rest of the manifest still loads. JSON output keeps commands bare.

examples.label: Typical

notes.text: In global mode: a manifest loads the same way when users install your package for their computer, beside the global CLI, and then applies in folders outside any project; inside a project, only if the project installs it. Peer ranges for `@astryxdesign/core` and `@astryxdesign/cli` are checked against the global CLI's release. See {@link namespace:global} and {@link generic:global-integrations}.

The provider name defaults to the package name in package.json. During a rename, set `providerId` to the old package name so the IDs of what the package already contributed stay the same. The package version always comes from package.json.

`agentDocs.append` may contain at most eight lines. Each line is a trimmed, non-blank string of at most 240 Unicode code points with no line separators, control characters, NUL, or Astryx/XDS managed-marker text. The configured project may contain at most 32 integration lines total. Write each command in a line as a bare `astryx` command; the managed block says once, before your lines, how the app starts the CLI.

Set `cliCommand` only when your users run the CLI with a command other than their package manager's, such as `acme astryx`. The CLI picks the command it prints in this order: the `cliCommand` of the loaded integrations when they name one command, then the command a host tool names, then the package manager's. Two different `cliCommand` values cancel out, and `{@command doctor}` warns in its `cli-command` check. See `{@command docs authoring/building-blocks/configuration/cli-command}`.

A themes root is version-gated: an older CLI lists and adds none of its themes. Depending on its age, that CLI ignores `themes` with an `unknown_manifest_key` warning and loads every other contribution kind, reports the root as invalid because it expects the earlier `manifest.json` theme catalog, or, if it is old enough to treat an unknown field as an error, rejects the whole manifest, so the package contributes nothing there.

Validate the manifest with `{@command doctor integration validate}`. At the load boundary, a known field of the wrong type is an error, issuesUrl and docsiteUrl must be valid URLs, and unknown fields become warnings so an older CLI can still load the fields it understands. Before publishing, also run `templates`, `components`, and `docs` under the same `doctor integration` group. Those leaves compare authored identities with Core and explain whether an overlap is intentional or needs a rename.

doc.name: discover
doc.summary: Browse and search integrations: the ones you have and the ones you could add
doc.description: Lists what this project has, the integrations it loads and the official packages it declares, then what it could add: the official Astryx packages first, then whatever its discover sources list, with what each one adds. Inside a project, integrations installed for the computer, beside the CLI installed for it, are listed as ones the project could add, with its install command; outside one they load. A package query shows one package: what it adds, every version a source knows, and the command that adds it. An @scope/name/Component path prints an installed component's doc; any other item path shows that item. Anything else, even an exact component name, searches every item and package and lists the matches. Discover only reads: your package manager installs, updates, and removes packages.

doc.name: docs
doc.summary: Print reference docs
doc.description: Reads the reference docs one level at a time: with no topic it lists every topic; a topic lists its sections, each with the key to read it by (a topic with one section prints whole); a topic plus a section prints that section; `--full` prints the whole topic, as does `--dense`. With `--json`, a topic returns its whole doc, as docs() does, and `--index` its section index. A route opens a node of the docs tree: `cli` lists its guides and reference, `cli/api/functions` lists every API function, and `cli/api/functions/search` prints one. A namespace plus a section prints that section from the one guide below it that has it (`{@command docs layout side-panels}`). `--depth` reads as far down the tree as you ask, from the doc alone (0) to everything below it (all), and with it `--detail` sets how much of each doc below shows: one line (brief, the default), its sections (compact), or all of it (full).

options.description: List the topic's sections and their keys, even for a topic with one section
Print the whole topic instead of its sections (text; `--json` returns the whole topic unless --index). Cannot be set with --index

How many levels of the docs tree to read below a namespace: 0 for the namespace alone, 1 for its children (what a read without --depth shows), all for everything below it. On the topic list, where a namespace otherwise lists alone, it names the docs below each one by the route that opens them, one line each. With it on a namespace read, --detail sets how much of each doc below shows: brief (one line each, the default), compact (with its sections), or full; the topic list is one line per doc whatever the detail

Every route in the docs tree, one line each
The integration guides as one read

exitCodes.when: success

doc.name: doctor integration components
doc.summary: Check integration component names, replacements, and documented props
doc.description: Compares one local or installed integration with Core component names. A conflict is allowed and exits successfully, but the report recommends renaming and gives the exact --package command for an intentional overlap. It also checks each component's replaces: in a package that declares the CLI range that turns replacement on, a missing Core target, an invalid value, a component named after a different Core component, or two replacements for one Core component is an error. In a package without that range they are warnings, with a warning for each such component, naming the range to declare. Then it compares each component doc's props with the component's TypeScript props, using the project's own `typescript` (or, where `typescript` is missing or has no JavaScript compiler API, as TypeScript 7 does, the `@typescript/typescript6` it installs), and warns about a documented prop the code lacks, a prop the package declares that the doc omits, a wrong `required`, and a type that does not match where both sides read exactly (it lists every other documented type as not compared, with the reason). Without TypeScript it prints one line saying the comparison was skipped. It also warns on each `{@link}` in a component doc's text that names no doc.

args.name: package
args.description: Installed integration package name; omit to check the package in the current directory.

exitCodes.when: the check completed; component name conflicts, replaces findings for a package without the CLI range, props that differ from the code, and links that name no doc are warnings
the integration is invalid, Core cannot be resolved, or a package that declares the CLI range has an invalid replaces

doc.name: doctor integration docs
doc.summary: Check an integration's docs: the docs tree they add, every link, and overlaps with Core topics
doc.description: Checks the docs tree the package adds, every link in its docs, and overlaps with Core topics. Intentional replacements and extensions are information. A same-name topic without `replaces` or `extends` is an accidental conflict and fails until the author declares the relationship or renames it. It also lists each pair of topics (two of the package, or one of them and a Core topic other than the one it replaces) that repeat 10 or more words of prose word for word, each padding phrase and low-density topic, and each written `{@command docs <name>}` that should be a link, each as a warning (`copied_passage`, `doc_fluff`, `stray_doc_pointer`; exit 0, and `integration check --strict` fails on it). See {@link generic:check-your-docs}.

args.name: package
args.description: Installed integration package name; omit to check the package in the current directory.

exitCodes.when: all Core overlaps are explicitly declared or no overlap exists
an overlap is accidental, a doc is invalid, a namespace or placement fails, or a reference block cannot include what it names. A link that names no doc is a warning, and does not change the exit code

doc.name: doctor integration templates
doc.summary: Validate integration template replacements and Core id overlaps
doc.description: Validates one local or installed integration against the built-in Core page and block template ids. Intentional replacements are informational and name the command for selecting the Core original. Missing targets, ambiguous replacements, and invalid declarations are errors; undeclared same-id overlaps remain warnings that require package selection.

args.name: package

exitCodes.when: replacement declarations are valid; undeclared id conflicts are warnings

doc.name: doctor integration validate
doc.summary: Validate an integration manifest and its contributions
doc.description: Validates one integration at a time: the local package rooted at cwd, or an installed package resolved by name. It schema-checks the manifest, verifies every declared contribution root, and reports every finding. Safe as a CI gate. It then checks every doc the package ships under its roots against the published authoring type for its kind, with the project's own `typescript` (or, where `typescript` is missing or has no JavaScript compiler API, as TypeScript 7 does, the `@typescript/typescript6` it installs), and warns about each field that does not match, naming the field and a fix. A doc it cannot fully check is listed with the reason, and test fixtures under `__tests__` in the components or docs root are counted, not checked. Without TypeScript it prints one line saying the docs were not type-checked. Outside a package, with no package name it writes nothing and reports one no_package issue (exit 1); a package name is looked up as it is in a project.

args.name: package
args.description: Installed integration package name; omit to validate the package in the current directory.

exitCodes.when: no error-severity issues (warnings, including doc type findings, are allowed)
one or more error-severity issues

In a project, the project's version of Astryx runs it, whichever astryx command you start. See {@link namespace:global} and {@link generic:global-integrations}.

doc.name: doctor
doc.summary: Diagnose Astryx projects and integration packages
doc.description: Runs read-only project health diagnostics by default: Node version, @astryxdesign/core install and version alignment, theme packages, generated app themes when present, earlier copied-theme migration, config, integrations (every one astryx.config names must load, linked without a config entry, provider identity, contribution issues), agent docs, core peer dependencies, package manager, the docs the CLI reads, the newest release the computer knows of, with the install and upgrade commands when the project's release is older, and every `astryx` command on the search path, warning when the first one is not the Astryx CLI or predates the hand-off. It writes nothing, but loading astryx.config runs that file's code. The `integration` subcommands provide authoring checks for one integration package. Outside a project it checks the computer instead: the Node version, the release that answered, the newest release this computer knows of, with the command that upgrades the CLI installed for the computer when it is older, the astryx commands on the search path, the integrations installed for the computer (warning about one it skips), and whether the computer-level agent text (`{@command init --user}`) is present, matches this release, was edited, or is turned off (info only); when that text names `astryx` and no `astryx` command is on the search path, apart from a package runner's own copy, it says so and names the install step the text records, or npm's when it records none. It never fails a check because the folder has no project.

exitCodes.when: no checks failed (warnings are allowed)

notes.text: In global mode: outside a project, doctor checks your computer instead of a folder: `node-version`, `answering-release` (the version that answered), `newest-release`, `cli-on-path` (every astryx command on your PATH), `computer-integrations` (integrations installed globally), and `computer-agent-text` (the agent guide). It never fails a check because the folder has no project. In a project, the project's version of Astryx runs it, whichever astryx command you start. See {@link namespace:global} and {@link generic:who-answers}.

doc.name: init
doc.summary: Initialize the design system in your project
doc.description: Non-interactive project setup (no prompts, so it behaves the same for humans, agents, and CI). By default it writes the agent-docs block, including guidance from configured integrations, to AGENTS.md and to the Claude Code file the project has (CLAUDE.md, else .claude/CLAUDE.md; when CLAUDE.md exists, a block in .claude/CLAUDE.md is removed, unless the project ignores CLAUDE.md, in which case a .claude/CLAUDE.md the project commits keeps a copy), and a one-line import of AGENTS.md to GEMINI.md unless GEMINI.md already imports it. It then prints getting-started steps. Agent docs go to the project root: the nearest folder at or above this one whose package.json declares an @astryxdesign package, else the nearest with any package.json, else this folder. The search stops at a repository root and never counts the home folder. In the home folder, or in a settings folder in it such as ~/.gemini outside a project, no agent docs are written. Every folder of the home folder whose name starts with a dot is a settings folder, and such a folder itself never counts as a project, even with a package.json; a project inside one, such as an agent worktree with its own package.json, works. The managed block is written whatever ignore rules or generated markers say; the text around it is never changed. --features and --all print only the chosen features' guidance (no getting-started steps); the theme feature also writes an annotated theme template. Outside a project it writes the same files but prints no step that sets up a project: no getting-started steps, and no step that adds a theme to an app. --user writes the computer-level agent text instead (see the flag), in any folder, and touches nothing in the folder. The CLI installed for the computer also keeps that text current in the background, unless --user --remove-agents turned it off; package install scripts, project setup, and upgrade never write it.

options.description: Comma-separated features: agents (agent docs), theme (writes theme.template.ts), template (prints the page-building commands; writes no file). An unknown feature exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_FEATURE. Refused with --all or --remove-agents

Remove the managed block from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, .hermes.md and HERMES.md, at the project root (where init writes them) and in this folder (deleting AGENTS.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md when only init's heading is left, and GEMINI.md when nothing is left) and do nothing else. Below the project root, a project-root agent file whose block resolves outside the project is left as it is, with a note. --features, --all, --agent and --agent-docs-path are refused; a file written with --agent-docs-path keeps its block

Write or refresh the computer-level agent text instead of setting up the folder: one skill file, ~/.agents/skills/astryx/SKILL.md, which most coding agents read, linked into the skill folders of agents that read only their own (~/.claude/skills always; Kiro, Windsurf, Letta, Xcode's coding assistant, and ~/.config/agents/skills when that folder exists): a folder symlink with a relative target, a junction on Windows, or a copy where neither can be made. Continue, whose scanner skips links, gets a managed copy, refreshed with the file. It tells agents anywhere on the computer that Astryx is there, when it is relevant, and to start with `astryx search`. Records the links it made in astryx/settings.json in the per-user configuration folder, so removal removes exactly those; the CLI installed for the computer refreshes the file in the background after each upgrade. Works in any folder. A file without the Astryx markers, one edited since Astryx wrote it, or a symlink, is kept as it is, and so is anything at a link target that Astryx did not create. Warns, and still writes, when no `astryx` command on the computer runs the Astryx CLI. With --remove-agents it removes the file, the links, and the copy instead and records that the text is turned off. --features, --all, --agent and --agent-docs-path are refused

Target AI tool for agent docs: claude (CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md, else creates .claude/CLAUDE.md), cursor (.cursorrules if present, else AGENTS.md), codex and muse (AGENTS.md), hermes (.hermes.md or HERMES.md if present, else AGENTS.md), all (every existing agent doc except GEMINI.md, which keeps its one-line import of AGENTS.md, else AGENTS.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md). With claude and all, when CLAUDE.md gets the block, .claude/CLAUDE.md gets none and a block already there is removed, unless the project ignores CLAUDE.md: then a .claude/CLAUDE.md the project commits gets a copy too, with claude and all alike. An unknown tool exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_AGENT. Used only when agent docs are installed (the default, --all, or --features agents); --agent-docs-path takes precedence.

Explicit file path(s) for agent docs, inside the project; takes precedence over --agent. If any path is outside the project, no agent docs are written and the command exits 1. A path in the home folder itself, or in a settings folder in it outside a project (such as ~/.claude or ~/.claude/hooks), is refused with a note (exit 0), and nothing is written. Used only when agent docs are installed

doc.name: integration check
doc.summary: The CI check for an integration package's own build: every source check, run in continuous integration or a typecheck script, against the package in the current folder
doc.description: Takes no package argument: it runs the four `doctor integration` checks, `validate`, `components`, `templates`, and `docs`, against the integration package in the current folder, which is where its own build runs it. It prints each result as that check prints it, then a summary with the errors, warnings, and skipped work of each, and exits 1 when any of the four would exit 1 on its own. With `--strict` it also exits 1 on any warning and on any check, or comparison within a check, that did not run, such as a package with no `astryx.integration.*` or a comparison skipped because the project has no TypeScript, or prop types not judged because its TypeScript is older than 4.8: it adds no check, and lists each of those again as an error, after the checks, in their own issue format. That is the line for the package's own build, so its docs, types, and links stay in sync: run it as a `ci` step, or add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && astryx integration check --strict"` to the scripts in package.json. Its exit codes and JSON are a contract for the builds that run it: a new check, or a new failure code, joins only in a minor release that names it in the release notes. A patch can still ship a Core component, template, or CLI topic whose name conflicts with one of yours. Run `integration check` on every build; run `integration verify` before you publish, to check that the packed package works in an app. To check an installed integration by name, run the `doctor integration` subcommands with its package name. Outside a package, it writes nothing, `validate` reports one `no_package` issue, and it exits 1.

options.description: Also exit 1 on any warning and on any check that did not run. A new check or failure code joins only in a minor release, named in the release notes; until then, a malformed `cliCommand` is reported as a note (`invalid_cli_command`) that fails nothing.

Also count the findings the next minor release turns into warnings (the notes marked `next`) as warnings now, so `--strict --next` fails on them. Run it to fix them ahead of the release; every run says how many there are.

doc.name: upgrade
doc.summary: Update your code after upgrading Astryx, and refresh ShadCN-copied components
doc.description: Migrates project source from a previous Astryx version to the installed one by running the registered codemods, and refreshes the fully rendered managed agent-docs block when Core or configured integration guidance changes. Dry-run by default. --apply writes codemod and receipt changes, runs hooks, then refreshes agent docs. Anything a post-codemod hook prints goes to stderr, so stdout carries only the result. Run from a folder inside a project, it upgrades that project and names files in the result relative to the folder you ran it in. ShadCN-copied compositions are checked automatically during a normal upgrade, or alone with --registry. Outside a project, --list lists the codemods this release ships and --registry finds no copied compositions to update; a migration writes nothing and fails with ERR_VERSION_DETECT, because no installed Core names its target.

options.description: Previous version before the dependency upgrade; required unless --list or --registry is set. The target is the installed @astryxdesign/core version, or legacy @xds/core when @astryxdesign/core is not installed
Write changes to disk; without it, the run is a dry run
Run codemods even if --from is newer than the installed version

Run only the named codemod. Optional codemods run only when named here; a normal run skips them. Also skips the check of ShadCN-copied compositions. An unknown name exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_CODEMOD when the version range has codemods
Exclude named codemods (repeatable). Re-run past a failed codemod by skipping it.
Explicit integration specifier (repeatable). Resolved beneath node_modules; absolute paths and `.` or `..` segments are rejected.

Install jscodeshift when it is missing. Without it, a missing jscodeshift fails the command with ERR_DEP_MISSING

Only update ShadCN-copied compositions from their install receipts: unchanged files are updated, edits that do not overlap are merged, and conflicts are left untouched; --from is not required. Combining it with --list, --from, --force, --codemod, --skip-codemod, --integration or --install-deps exits 1 with ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT

exitCodes.when: success, including complete dry-run previews and runs whose only findings are manual migrations

missing or invalid --from, --registry with --list or a migration flag, a --path escape, no installed @astryxdesign/core (or legacy @xds/core), jscodeshift missing and not installed by --install-deps, an astryx.config that fails validation and that no pending config codemod repairs, an unreadable or invalid protection declaration, a protected file that still requires a codemod change, a generated file that must be regenerated, an unknown codemod, a codemod or post-codemod hook failure, or unresolved registry items

notes.text: In global mode: in a project, upgrade runs the codemods of the project's own CLI, whichever astryx command you start; in a project with no CLI of its own, the astryx command you started runs them, so install the CLI at the new Core's version first (`{@command doctor}` prints the command). Outside a project, `--list` lists this version's codemods, `--registry` finds no copied compositions, and a migration writes nothing and stops with `ERR_VERSION_DETECT`. See {@link namespace:global} and {@link generic:who-answers}.
A CLI older than your Core

Core codemods ship inside the CLI, so a CLI older than the installed @astryxdesign/core has none for the releases after its own version. upgrade then says it cannot finish, never reports your code as up to date, and prints the same upgrade pinned to the CLI release that matches your Core, such as `cd <project> && npx @astryxdesign/cli@<core-version> upgrade --from <old-version> --path <source-dir> --apply`. It changes to the folder this run used and names the directory it scanned as an absolute path, both with symbolic links resolved, so pasted from any folder it upgrades the same code. It is written for a POSIX shell (sh, bash, zsh), or for PowerShell on Windows, with each argument quoted for that shell; cmd.exe is not a target. The codemods this CLI has still run. It exits 0, so a script checks the JSON: the result carries `cliBehindCore` with `cliVersion` (the newest release this CLI has codemods for) and `command`.
Protected files

Codemods never write to a file your project marks as generated, vendored, or ignored. upgrade reads these marks from the files on disk, so the answer is the same with any version control, or none. A file is protected when:

items: a `.gitattributes` file marks it `linguist-generated` or `linguist-vendored`
its leading comment says `@generated`, `@partially-generated`, or `Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.`
a `.gitignore`, or the `.hgignore` at the project root, excludes it
it is an installed dependency (such as anything in `node_modules`), is inside `.git`, `.hg`, or `.sl`, is a symbolic link, or is outside the project

notes.text: upgrade does not scan installed dependencies or version-control folders at all, including through a symbolic link: a symlinked `node_modules`, or a link whose target is inside one or inside a package store such as `.yarn/cache`, is skipped. Other symbolically linked folders are scanned so a change they need is reported, but nothing is written through them.

Rules work as they do in Git: a later rule wins, so `linguist-generated=false` or a `!` line in an ignore file returns a file to normal handling. A folder name such as `dist` or `generated` protects nothing by itself. If a protection file cannot be read or parsed, upgrade stops with ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTION_SOURCE before it writes anything.

notes.code:
# .gitattributes
generated/** linguist-generated=true
vendor/** linguist-vendored=true

# A later rule returns one authored file to normal handling
generated/hand-authored.ts linguist-generated=false

notes.text: When a codemod would change a protected file, upgrade makes the change only in memory and leaves the file as it is. The rest of the upgrade goes ahead. With --apply, your other files are written, then upgrade runs the `hooks.postCodemod` commands from astryx.config (see `{@command docs authoring config}`) and checks the protected files again. If one still needs the change, the run is incomplete: it exits 1, prints ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED with each file and the rule that protects it, and does not refresh the agent docs. Regenerate or edit those files, then run the same upgrade again. A dry run reports the same files and writes nothing.

With --json, the receipt says `complete: false` and `errorCode: "ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED"`. `modifiedFiles` lists the files upgrade changed (or would change), and `protectedFiles` lists each blocked file with its `reasons`, `declarations` (the rules that protect it), `codemods`, and `commands`. A generated file can name the command that rebuilds it on a `Command:` line in its header, such as `// Command: pnpm run gen:panel`; upgrade prints it as `Regenerate with: <command>` and lists it in `commands`.

A protected file a codemod cannot parse, such as a vendored bundle written for another toolchain, cannot need a change the codemod can prove, and upgrade never writes it. upgrade skips it, lists it under `declinedCandidates` with the parse error and where it occurred, and carries on; on its own it does not fail the run. If another codemod in the same upgrade still requires a change to that file (the 0.6.0 theme selector migration, for one, adds a TODO comment above a selector it cannot parse), the file is listed once, under `protectedFiles`, and the run is incomplete as for any protected file. A file upgrade owns that does not parse still fails the run with ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED.
Manual migrations and regeneration

Some changes a codemod can find but not make. upgrade lists them in the result, so a script can keep the rest of the run and act on each. Code a codemod can identify but cannot migrate safely is a manual migration: upgrade lists each file with its line, the codemod and what to change, finishes the run, and exits 0. With --json they are in `declinedCandidates`, one row per file (each finding in `reason` starts with `manual migration needed (<codemod>):`, and a file with several findings lists them all, joined by `; `), and `complete` stays true. A generated file that must be rebuilt is listed in `regenerate` with the command that rebuilds it, such as `astryx theme build`: a protected generated file a codemod still needs to change (also in `protectedFiles`), or a generated output a codemod found out of date (also in `protectedFiles`, with the rule that protects it, when the project marks it generated). With --apply, upgrade runs your `hooks.postCodemod` commands and checks again. If a protected file still needs rebuilding, the run is incomplete exactly as for any protected file: it exits 1 and the result says `complete: false` and `errorCode: "ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED"`. If a file nothing protects still needs rebuilding, no protected file is in the way: the codemod could not make a required change, so it is also in `errors` and the run fails with `ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED`, as described below. Either way, rebuild it, then run the same upgrade again. When a codemod also failed, the failure is reported as below, and the receipt it carries still lists `declinedCandidates` and `regenerate`, unless a protected file to regenerate also remains, in which case the run returns `ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED` with the failure in `errors`.
A failed codemod

When a codemod or a `hooks.postCodemod` command fails, upgrade still makes every other change, exits 1 with ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED, and does not refresh the agent docs. With --json, the result is the usual error, `{"error": ..., "code": "ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED"}`, plus a `receipt`: the same fields a finished run returns, with `complete: false`, each failure in `errors`, and every file upgrade changed (or would change) in `modifiedFiles`, so a script can review, keep, or revert them. An error that stops the run after codemods have written files, such as an astryx.config that fails validation, carries a `receipt` too. Rerun past a failed codemod with --skip-codemod.
